Half of Dave Carter and Tracy Grammer, who toured the U.S. with Joan Baez in 2002; Drum Hat Buddha (2001) met critical success. Her 2005 solo Flower of Avalon has Mary Chapin Carpenter on backing vocals.
Piedmont-blues fingerpicker: third at the National Finger Style Guitar Championship in 2000 and 2003, Blues Music Award nominee for Acoustic Artist 2008, Independent Music Awards winner 2010.

2010.headline: The year string-band folk and Americana were the sound, and the future Hadestown writer came
2010.story: 2010 was a roots year. Typhoon, The Black Lillies and Sallie Ford were young bands: the Black Lillies reached the Grand Ole Opry in 2011, and Ford played Letterman that August. Bonnie "Prince" Billy, Michael Hurley and T-Model Ford brought decades of records. Anaïs Mitchell's Hadestown later won the Tony. Dr. Dog came back.

scenes.name: Progressive bluegrass & string bands
scenes.blurb: Acoustic virtuosity moved from the bluegrass circuit toward the Grammys, with Punch Brothers and Decemberists-bred Black Prairie on the bluegrass chart.

scenes.name: Indie folk & chamber-pop storytelling
scenes.blurb: Songwriters with a theatrical or literary streak, from a folk opera to an eleven-piece band, found wider rooms.

scenes.name: Americana & country-soul
scenes.blurb: Texas songwriting awards, Knoxville country-soul and Portland swing drew Americana, Opry and late-night TV attention.
acts: The everybodyfields' Jill Andrews and Sam Quinn

scenes.name: Lo-fi, indie rock & old-time outsiders
scenes.blurb: Label-signed indie bands shared the farm with Folkways-era veterans and a Delta blues original.

2010.legends_note: Bonnie "Prince" Billy, Michael Hurley and T-Model Ford each had decades of recorded work behind them before choosing the farm; Johnny Cash covered Oldham's I See a Darkness, and Hurley's first album came out on Folkways in the early 1960s.

acts.proof: White Lighter (2013) ranked No. 28 in NPR's album poll and No. 37 on Paste's list; the band later played Lollapalooza and Outside Lands.
Made their Grand Ole Opry debut June 17, 2011 and have appeared more than 35 times, described as a record for an independent act.
Signed to Partisan Records in 2011 and played Late Show with David Letterman in August 2011, a year after Pickathon.
Will Oldham debuted in 1993 as Palace Brothers; Johnny Cash covered I See a Darkness on American III with Oldham on backing vocals.
Discovered by Fat Possum in 1995; five Fat Possum albums from 1997 to 2008 and the 1997 documentary Juke.
Debut First Songs was recorded for Folkways in 1963-64; Have Moicy! was Robert Christgau's favorite album of its year, and his songs scored Deadwood.
Hadestown won the 2019 Tony for Best Original Score and the cast album the 2020 Grammy; the 2010 album placed No. 63 on Paste's best indie folk albums.
All Ashore won the 2019 Grammy for Best Folk Album; leader Chris Thile was a 2012 MacArthur Fellow.
Formed in 2007 by Decemberists Chris Funk and Nate Query; Feast of the Hunter's Moon (Sugar Hill, 2010) peaked No. 4 on the US Bluegrass chart.
She Left Me for Jesus was the 2008 Americana Song of the Year; KMAG YOYO reached No. 67 on the Billboard 200; Chances Are was a 2016 Grammy nominee for Best Country Song.
Signed to Sub Pop in 2002; Eric D. Johnson toured with The Shins 2006-2010; Tripper (2011) reached the Billboard Heatseekers top 15.
Founding-era Be Good Tanyas member; Indian Ocean was on the 2015 Polaris Music Prize long list; solo debut Obadiah came out July 2010.
Formed from DeYarmond Edison after Justin Vernon left to make Bon Iver; Pitchfork called Gather, Form & Fly 'a headily absorbing, occasionally unsettling listen.'
Taped Austin City Limits in June 2009; Arrow (2012) reached No. 78 on a US albums chart (chart not named on the page).
Uncut named Post to Wire (2004) and The Fitzgerald (2005) Albums of the Month; a 2016 album reached No. 65 on the UK chart.
Paranoid Cocoon (Jan. 27, 2009) was their debut on Suicide Squeeze; critics compared it to Johnny Cash, Mazzy Star and Beach House.
Brooklyn trio formed in 2008; Smithsonian Folkways released their album Old Man Below made with New Lost City Ramblers founder John Cohen.
Co-founded The everybodyfields; his song T.V.A. won the 2005 Chris Austin Songwriting Contest at MerleFest and the band played Bonnaroo in 2008.

2011.headline: The year Future Islands and Sturgill Simpson's band played before they broke out
2011.story: Pickathon 2011 booked Future Islands, Strand of Oaks, Whitey Morgan & the 78’s and Sunday Valley, the band Sturgill Simpson fronted, before any of them were known. Mavis Staples, fresh off a Grammy, headed the legends. Wye Oak's Civilian topped The A.V. Club's 2011 list, and Pokey LaFarge returned.

scenes.name: Indie rock & dream-pop
scenes.blurb: Wye Oak's Civilian ranked on four 2011 year-end lists; Future Islands and Strand of Oaks were still playing small rooms.

scenes.name: Americana & outlaw country
scenes.blurb: Sunday Valley was Sturgill Simpson's first act on the farm; Ray Wylie Hubbard and Eilen Jewell worked the roots end.

scenes.name: Soul & Latin funk
scenes.blurb: A fresh Grammy winner, a veteran soul singer and Austin's Latin-funk family shared the stage.

scenes.name: Songwriters' songwriters
scenes.blurb: Critics' favorites who stayed in clubs and listening rooms.

2011.legends_note: Mavis Staples came months after winning her first competitive solo Grammy, with Lee Fields and Ray Wylie Hubbard choosing a reverent crowd too.

acts.proof: Sturgill Simpson's band won Emerging Artist of the Year at the 2014 Americana awards, then Best Country Album at the 59th Grammys (Feb. 12, 2017) and played SNL in January 2017.
Performed 'Seasons (Waiting on You)' on Letterman March 3, 2014; Singles ranked No. 22 on Pitchfork's 2014 list and peaked No. 40 on the Billboard 200.
HEAL (2014, Dead Oceans) was named one of the best albums of 2014; the band made its TV debut on Late Night with Seth Meyers that year.
Won the Grammy for Best Americana Album for You Are Not Alone in 2011, her first competitive solo Grammy; Rock Hall inductee with the Staple Singers (1999).
Recording since 1969; songs placed in Suits, Magic Mike XXL and Atlanta, and additional vocals on the James Brown biopic Get On Up (2014).
Inducted into the Texas Heritage Songwriters Association Hall of Fame in 2018; 'Up Against the Wall, Redneck Mother' is described as a perennial anthem.
Civilian was No. 1 on The A.V. Club's 2011 albums list, No. 8 Magnet, No. 17 Treble, No. 18 Paste; No. 1 on Billboard Heatseekers.
Apocalypse was No. 23 on Pitchfork's and Mojo's 2011 lists, No. 25 on Uncut's, and No. 39 on Pitchfork's best albums of the 2010s.
Won the Grammy for Best Latin Rock, Alternative or Urban Album for El Existential at the 53rd Grammys, early 2011.
Formed in Portland in 2009 and named Portland's best new band by Willamette Week in 2011; Divisionary followed on Partisan Records in 2014.
In the Future was a 2008 Polaris Music Prize finalist; Wilderness Heart was longlisted for the 2011 Polaris.
Joined The Shins in 2011, toured with The Black Keys 2014-15, and produced Foxygen, Damien Jurado and Nathaniel Rateliff & the Night Sweats.
Year of Meteors was a New York Times critic's choice (2005); inducted into the Oregon Music Hall of Fame in October 2024.
The Grupo Fantasma offshoot's Brown Sabbath covers (2014) drew praise from NPR, AllMusic and Rolling Stone, and from Ozzy Osbourne; the band has played Bonnaroo.
Signed to Barsuk in 2003; wrote 'The Sinking Belle' for Sunn O)))'s Altar, which Pitchfork called the album's centerpiece and masterpiece.
Won first prize at the 2007 Podunk Bluegrass Festival band contest; bassist Bridget Kearney left in 2012 for Lake Street Dive.
Tim Rutili's band, active since 1997 on Thrill Jockey and Dead Oceans; The New York Times called Roots & Crowns enthralling.
Grammy-nominated in Best Zydeco or Cajun Music Album (Wikipedia lists nominations from 2007 on); six State Department world tours.

In 2011 he was on the road most of the year, grinding it out in small bars and clubs. By 2018 Hard Times and White Lines hit No. 2 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and he played the Ryman Auditorium in Nashville for the first time.

2012.headline: The year indie rock, duo Americana and Louisiana roots sent future breakouts to the farm
2012.story: Five first-time discoveries came in 2012: The War on Drugs, Lake Street Dive, Shovels & Rope, The Barr Brothers and Cass McCombs. The first four broke out within a few years; Spin ranked two of McCombs’s 2011 albums among its fifty best. Phosphorescent, Thee Oh Sees and Bombino arrived as critics' favorites. Dr. Dog and Langhorne Slim returned.

scenes.name: Indie rock & garage
scenes.blurb: The War on Drugs and Thee Oh Sees played a year before the albums critics ranked at or near the top; Cass McCombs and White Denim came too.

scenes.name: Duo Americana & songwriters
scenes.blurb: Shovels & Rope released O' Be Joyful days before the farm and won Americana Honors in 2013; Phosphorescent and Neko Case followed the same path.

scenes.name: Soul, jazz-pop & retro R&B
scenes.blurb: Lake Street Dive's Jackson 5 cover went viral in May 2012; The Barr Brothers and Kitty, Daisy & Lewis brought other roots-pop.

scenes.name: Global & Louisiana roots
scenes.blurb: Bombino, Hot 8 Brass Band, Lost Bayou Ramblers and Los Cojolites each later drew Grammy nominations or wins.
acts: Lost Bayou Ramblers ft Gordon Gano

acts.proof: Lost in the Dream (2014) was No. 1 on Paste, Consequence, Uncut and Q lists and No. 2 on Stereogum and Guardian; A Deeper Understanding won the 2018 Grammy for Best Rock Album.
Viral Jackson 5 cover went up May 2012, three months before the farm. Red Rocks headline debut Sept 6, 2018; first Madison Square Garden headline Sept 14, 2024.
O' Be Joyful came out July 31, 2012, days before the farm. They won Emerging Artist and Song of the Year at the 2013 Americana Honors and played Letterman on Jan 30, 2013.
Juno nominations for Adult Alternative Album in 2013, 2015 and 2018, plus Red Rocks and Osheaga main stage appearances.
Middle Cyclone (2009) peaked No. 3 on the Billboard 200, her first top ten, with two Grammy nominations. Told the Pickathon crowd it was the most amazing place she had played.
Muchacho (2013) drew rave reviews, Pitchfork's among them, and peaked No. 59 on the Billboard 200.
Floating Coffin (April 2013) drew universal acclaim, with strong reviews from Uncut and Pitchfork.
Nomad (Nonesuch, 2013, produced by Dan Auerbach) debuted No. 1 on Billboard World; Deran earned a 2019 Grammy nomination for Best World Music Album, the first for a Nigerien artist.
Kalenda won the 2018 Grammy for Best Regional Roots Music Album; they won again in 2024 with the Louisiana Philharmonic.
Béla Fleck & Abigail Washburn won the 2016 Grammy for Best Folk Album at the 58th Grammy Awards.
SPIN ranked Wit's End and Humor Risk together at No. 25 on its 50 best albums of 2011. Humor Risk drew strong reviews, Pitchfork's among them.
Two Grammy nominations for Best Regional Mexican Music Album (Including Tejano): Sembrando Flores (2013) and Zapateando (2016).
Danny Paisley won IBMA Male Vocalist of the Year in 2016; the band won IBMA Song of the Year in 2009.
Rise & Shine (2010) was named Album of the Year by World Music Charts Europe.
Inducted into the Oregon Music Hall of Fame in 2021, alongside The Decemberists and Lifesavas.
Named Best New Band at the 2008 Austin Music Awards; opened for Wilco and played Bonnaroo in 2012.
Smoking in Heaven (2011) reached No. 145 in the UK; opened for Coldplay in North America and for Phish at The Gorge in 2011.
Played Mississippi in the 2017 Twin Peaks revival. Easy Way (2019) peaked No. 21 on Billboard Indie.
Ojos del Sol (2016) made NPR's Top 50 albums of 2016; Tiny Desk Concert in September 2019; Mujeres debuted No. 7 on Latin Pop Albums.
The Life & Times of... The Hot 8 Brass Band appears as a nominee in the 2014 Grammy Best Regional Roots Music Album list.
Debut awE naturalE (Sub Pop, March 2012) drew good reviews, Pitchfork's among them, and was No. 62 on MusicOMH's top 100 albums of 2012.

2013.headline: The year Sturgill Simpson, Shakey Graves, Ty Segall and Kurt Vile all first came
2013.story: Pickathon 2013 first booked Sturgill Simpson, Shakey Graves, Ty Segall, Kurt Vile, Parquet Courts and Jessica Pratt, none yet big. Sturgill won a Grammy and Shakey an Americana award within four years. Feist and Andrew Bird, already established, came anyway. Lake Street Dive returned.

scenes.name: Garage, psych & post-punk
scenes.blurb: Fuzz and basement punk took over indie, and critics rewarded it that year.

scenes.name: New outlaw country & roots
scenes.blurb: Country and Americana turned to loners and traditionalists; a Grammy and an Americana award followed within four years.

scenes.name: Indie songwriters & supergroups
scenes.blurb: Established indie names played the farm, from Feist to a Spoon and Wolf Parade supergroup near its end.

scenes.name: Roots from around the world
scenes.blurb: Zydeco, Appalachian and Malian guitar sat beside the rock bands.

2013.legends_note: Feist, fresh off a Polaris Prize and four Grammy nominations, and Andrew Bird chose a farm festival; Divine Fits played one of its last shows.

acts.proof: Won the 2017 Grammy for Best Country Album (A Sailor's Guide to Earth, also up for Album of the Year); it peaked No. 3 on the Billboard 200, three years after his self-released debut.
Won Emerging Artist of the Year at the 2015 Americana Honors & Awards; And the War Came peaked No. 44 on the Billboard 200 and he made his TV debut on Conan in Oct. 2014.
Twins hit No. 1 on the CMJ chart in Nov. 2012; Manipulator (2014) became his first Billboard 200 entry at No. 45, and later albums kept charting.
Wakin on a Pretty Daze ranked No. 5 on Consequence of Sound's, No. 8 on Uncut's, No. 10 on Spin's and No. 13 on Pitchfork's 2013 lists; peaked No. 47 on the Billboard 200.
Self-titled debut (Jan. 2013) peaked No. 64 on the Billboard 200 to strong reviews; later Americana Awards Duo/Group nominee, and Then Came the Morning reached No. 44.
Signs & Signifiers won Best Rock/Hard Rock Album at the 2012 Independent Music Awards; in 2022 he opened and played guitar on the Robert Plant and Alison Krauss tour.

2014.headline: The year Mac DeMarco, Angel Olsen and Courtney Barnett came through before the big rooms
2014.story: Pickathon 2014 booked the new indie class before it broke: Mac DeMarco with Salad Days weeks old, Angel Olsen ahead of a year-end list run, and Courtney Barnett after two EPs. Unknown Mortal Orchestra, Gregory Alan Isakov, Hiss Golden Messenger and Valerie June came up too. Jonathan Richman and Bobby Patterson were the legends. The War on Drugs, Parquet Courts and Shakey Graves returned.

2015.headline: Leon Bridges, Kamasi Washington and Joseph arrived before the world knew them
2015.story: Pickathon 2015 booked Leon Bridges before Coming Home hit No. 6, Kamasi Washington as The Epic landed, and Portland's Joseph two years before their Heatseekers No. 1. The Weather Station came six years before Ignorance topped Uncut’s 2021 list. Cloud Nothings, Ex Hex and Tune-Yards brought critics' favorites, and Tinariwen and Ernest Ranglin came as elders. Ty Segall and Hiss Golden Messenger returned.

Above them stood Jeff Tweedy, Yo La Tengo and King Sunny Adé, with critics' favorite Julia Holter. Ty Segall, Mac DeMarco and Kevin Morby came back.

2018.headline: The year outlaw country, soul and psych arrived before the rest of the world did
2018.story: In 2018 a Saskatchewan baritone, a Texas busker and a new Austin duo played the farm before their names traveled: Colter Wall, Charley Crockett, Black Pumas. Haley Heynderickx, Jamila Woods, Paul Cauthen and Kikagaku Moyo came before the best-of lists and bigger rooms that followed. The War and Treaty brought soul that later earned Grammy nominations. Built to Spill, Broken Social Scene and the Blind Boys of Alabama came as legends. Tinariwen and Shakey Graves returned.

Thee Sacred Souls, Faye Webster, Sampa The Great, Goth Babe, Soul Glo and Armand Hammer came as discoveries. Nubya Garcia, Sons of Kemet and Emma Jean Thackray showed London jazz at its peak,. 2023.headline: Two Asheville bands on the way up, a soul summer in the barns, and a Sunday Haley Heynderickx saved
2023.story: Wednesday and MJ Lenderman came out of the same Asheville scene, and both were still playing clubs when they got to the farm. By December Rat Saw God was album of the year at Paste and Stereogum, and a year later Manning Fireworks topped The New Yorker's list. The barns ran on soul, from Lee Fields, who cut his first single in 1969, to Say She She, whose “Astral Plane” became the song of the weekend. W.I.T.C.H. came from Zambia and gave the Woods a masterclass. And on Sunday, when COVID took Watchhouse off the bill, Haley Heynderickx said yes at the last minute and closed the Woods alone.

2024.headline: The year indie songwriters led, new jazz and hip-hop pushed in, and two favorites came back
2024.story: The sound of 2024 was the indie songwriter, from Geese and Water From Your Eyes to Kara Jackson, Ratboys, Jess Williamson and Joanna Sternberg, the albums critics had just crowned. New jazz and hip-hop pushed in beside them, with McKinley Dixon, Kassa Overall and Irreversible Entanglements. LA LOM brought the Latin groove. And two came back, ten and fourteen years on: Courtney Barnett and Bonnie “Prince” Billy. Off the music stages, novelist Willy Vlautin read on Sunday morning at the Windmill, two-time Grammy winner Lucy Kalantari played the Coyote stage, and Amy Miller hosted two nights of stand-up in the Lucky Barn.

2025.story: Pickathon's 25th year paired Grammy-level names, Taj Mahal and Portugal. The Man, with players still on small stages. Colby T. Helms, a 21-year-old Virginia country singer, is the discovery to watch. Jake Vaadeland won a Juno, East Nash Grass was named IBMA New Artist of the Year, and Dummy and Wild Pink brought critics' favorites. Too soon to call who breaks out.

Esther Rose and Ken Pomeroy made Stereogum's 2025 country list and Hannah Frances made Paste's top 50. Shakey Graves returned as a 2013 discovery. Too soon to call who breaks out.

2006.story: Pickathon moved to Pendarvis Farm in 2006. The Avett Brothers, on their first national tour and their first trip to Oregon, were the discovery. Iris DeMent, Greg Brown and C.J. Chenier were already established, and the Wailin' Jennys and the Wood Brothers were roots acts with credentials. Danny Barnes and Kelly Joe Phelps came back.

2017.headline: The year indie songwriters, soul and Americana all got their breakout
2017.story: Big Thief, Lucy Dacus and Tank and the Bangas first came to the farm in 2017, ahead of Grammy nominations and sold-out theaters. Marlon Williams, Pinegrove, Brent Cobb and Jalen Ngonda arrived before their breakouts. Charles Bradley played seven weeks before he died. Billy Strings and Ty Segall came back.

Raised on a steady diet of jungle and hardcore punk, she is known for her range and eclecticism.

DJ Maaxa is a music anthropologist, radio host, writer, and 25-year veteran behind the decks with roots in the Bay Area funk scene. Her work has been featured in SPIN, the SF Bay Guardian, shows on KMHD, and field studies throughout the Global South.
Allen “The Ambassador” Thayer is a music journalist, radio, and club DJ specializing in soul and funk-infused music scenes from around the world, with a specialty in Brazilian music.
DJ Queen Amygdala is a Portland-based all-vinyl DJ and synth musician in local bands Sylphide and The Soft Colors.
From Instant Nostalgia to Skeeter Valentine -- Sam Kelly Jr. has finally evolved into record collector and deep cut connoisseur: DJ MySpace. Hitting you with movers, groovers, rockers, and rollers.
Aside from Papi Fimbres playing in over a thousand bands in and around the city of Portland, Oregon, he also manages to find time to DJ when the opportunity arises.

Tom Humphrey has been hosting the weekly radio show, Backroad to Nowhere (Sundays, 6-7 p.m) on XRAY.fm Portland since the station’s inception in 2014 as well as DJing parties and pre-show sets at Pickathon since 2016.
Mod Fodder brings a banging mix of Mod music from the swinging '60s, punk-tinged '70s, and '80s revival, as well as some psychedelic Mod of the '90s.
Vinyl devotee and host of Manteca on KMHD, disco diablo spins genre-blurring sets full of thoughtful energy, and unexpected gems - all guided by a love of filling space with sound.
Tobias is a musician, audio engineer, DJ and designer living in Portland, OR. who’s been DJing, producing and engineering music over 25 years.
Eric Hedford aka DJ AQUAMAN is a musician and DJ based out of Portland, Oregon. Best known for his legendary SOUL STEW dance night at The Goodfoot and as the founding drummer in The Dandy Warhols.

DJ Honest John is a Portland-based party curator with roots in Miami who brings the heat wherever his needle drops. His sets weave together funky disco, bouncy boogie, and more smooth grooves to keep dance floors moving.
Mixes range from eccentric to essential soul music made for dancing.
Impact Sound is a DJ crew based in the Portland, consisting of DuMp-TrUcK, Yoni, Hep Greg, and Cory, specializing in reggae, ska, and rocksteady.

Katie Nguyen is a writer and comedian living in Portland, Oregon. Her writing has been featured in The New Yorker, you can hear her stand-up on SiriusXM radio, and she is a regular at Helium Comedy Club.
Hey I’m Ikes, let’s have a great laugh together. Love and peace oh and food oh and water and beer and stuff. Ohh a cider too. I can’t wait to be on your show.
Portland's Funniest Person of 2015 who started Pickathon comedy in 2016. She went on to a Comedy Central half-hour special, Last Comic Standing and CBS's After Midnight.
Described as Chris Farley meets Sam Kinison, Simon has captivated audiences all over the country with his one of a kind comedic style.

Ricci Armani is a stand up comedian, writer and the creator and co-host of the monthly sold out show “My Straight Friends." My Straight Friends is based out of The Comedy Store in LA and Emerald City in Seattle.

Patti Wheeler is a writer and storyteller from Hell, Michigan. Her work centers on the importance of finding community and loving deeply. She recently sold her house in Detroit and bought a minivan and a historic home in the suburbs in the same month.

2026.l: The Traveling Typist is an interactive performance artist focused on creating cherished memories and spreading joy using their fleet of vintage typewriters.
Christina and Andrés are 123 Andrés, the GRAMMY and Latin Grammy-winning duo for kids and families known for their interactive, high-energy shows.
We are a volunteer collective that creates educational art and events using science, comedy & play to educate & inspire people to be better stewards of our only home, Earth.

Stamp Collecting would call themselves an emo band if you asked, but will say it with a hesitancy born from years of inspiration across genres. A group of recently graduated seniors - catch 'em before they are flung to the corners of the United States.
Hola chicos, I'm Teacher Brittany. I was a professional actor-musician in NYC for many years and now I share music on my guitar through a Trauma-informed Lens with children, families and elders.
Shady Pines Radio is an award-winning nonprofit community radio station based in Portland, dedicated to energizing the local music and arts scene while showcasing amazing music from here and beyond.

2026.n: Family Square Dance: Steph Noll calling with Triple File
2026.l: Triple File is a band of three teens from Portland, OR, playing fiddle music from around the globe with twin fiddles and driving guitar. You can find them playing at regional festivals, farmers markets, square dances, and Céilís.
Adnauseam is a 4 piece grunge band with strong roots in the PNW scene. The young group blends the raw and unforgiving sound of the 90s while bringing their own heavy and emotional intensity.
Aaron Nigel Smith is a Grammy-nominated producer, composer, and educator who brings a vibrant, global-music-infused energy to the stage.
Flor Bromley is a GRAMMY® (2026) and Latin GRAMMY® (2023) nominated children’s music artist, originally from Peru, who brings a vibrant blend of music and storytelling to audiences of all ages.

Fyütch is a GRAMMY-winning artist, songwriter, producer, and educator, known for his empowering songs for all-ages. He has contributed to radio-charting songs and original compositions for TV and family media including Sesame Street.

2026.n: Mo Phillips and the Spaghetti Pants Dance Band
2026.l: Mo Phillips and The Spaghetti Pants Dance Band is a journey to unfettered goofballery. An interactive dance party that invites the bravest of the brave to bring every wiggle bone to the dance floor. Got Fish Feet? Bring 'em. A couch named Maria?

David DaCosta is a Dad, Author, Illustrator, and Multi-Disciplinary Designer with over 20 years experience in branding and marketing. He counts his New York upbringing, classic cartoons, and his family as a few of his many inspirations.
My Voice Music (MVM) is a nonprofit music organization based in SE Portland that empowers youth to share their stories and express themselves through music.
Giant puppets made by 350PDX, XRPDX and Making Earth Cool in celebration of our only home, Earth will soar and hop through the trees and up the hills of Pickathon!
Miss Josephine brings color and whimsy to Pickathon with fantastical face painting and sparkling bubbles🫧

Jared White, owner of Clinton Street Records, has spent over 30 years behind the booth cultivating a deep and versatile sound.
Originally from Albuquerque, Dan Yaker is a Portland-based DJ who has been busy collecting records and playing them for friends since 2007.
Based in Portland, Oregon, DJ Snacks spins an eclectic, record-heavy mix that feels like the ultimate shared playlist.
Dj Stray is a Portland based dj that has held numerous residencies in the city throughout the years while also being recognized nationally. In 2019 Stray appeared on Sway in the Morning on Sirius XM.

Flor Violenta is a Portland-based DJ spinning cumbia and other latin sounds for the dancefloor, moving between psychedelic, tropical, and electronic styles while highlighting new interpretations rooted in traditional rhythms.

Greasy ( Mat Griesse ) is a real record junkie and has been digging for under appreciated cuts since the late 80’s. He started DJing in Seattle around 1997 at nights like Truth and Soul Inc, Broken Beats, Deep Funk etc.
The Country Co Op is a country music DJ collective formed in 2017 and based in Portland Oregon.
Impact Sound is a DJ crew based in the Portland, consisting of DuMp-TrUcK, Yoni, Hep Greg, and Cory, specializing in reggae, ska, and rocksteady.
Joshua Limanjaya is a Portland-based DJ, producer, and founder of the TOKO TAPE label.
Nothing if not consistently reliable, Nathan Detroit has been shaking down dance floors and leaving no genre unturned in his 20+ years behind the decks.
Jesse Sugar Moore is a lifelong record collector, DJ, and half the creative force behind the record and art shop Broken Dreams in Portland's Alberta Arts District.

Hailing from the Oklahoma prarie and now based in Corvallis, Phreaker Fighter is a fresh face in Portland’s dance scene who takes great inspiration from the record slinging legends of Chicago and Detroit.
Brooklyn based Prince Klassen learned from their late 90s beginnings that music and art do not have to be linear in practice.
K Marie is a Portland-based curator of vibes known for her seamless, open-format sets that move effortlessly across genres.
Red Yarn (aka Andy Furgeson) is a Texas-born, Oregon-based family performer who weaves roots music and puppetry into engaging shows for all ages.

Tom Humphrey has been hosting the weekly radio show, Backroad to Nowhere (Sundays, 6-7 p.m) on XRAY.fm Portland since the station’s inception in 2014 as well as DJing parties and pre-show sets at Pickathon since 2016.
The Wayward Girls Soul Club is an all female DJ collective that has been serving their favorite records to venues in Portland and beyond since 2019.
Influenced by luminaries like Pete Rock, Edan and J-Live, spinitch is a "triple-threat" i.e. producer, MC, and DJ.

Center for Cassette Studies is a collective of two DJs, Karen and Jim, who started spinning together in 2016 at Freeform Portland community radio. Since then, the Center has aired live weekly at KFFP 98.3 FM and worldwide online.
Allen “The Ambassador” Thayer is a music journalist, radio, and club DJ specializing in soul and funk-infused music scenes from around the world, with a specialty in Brazilian music.
DJ Dentside is a country music DJ known for bringing honky-tonk energy to the dance floor, regularly hosting lively nights at the Kenton Club.

DJ Maaxa is a music anthropologist, radio host, writer, and 25-year veteran behind the decks with roots in the Bay Area funk scene. Her work has been featured in SPIN, the SF Bay Guardian, shows on KMHD, and field studies throughout the Global South.
His sound is an eclectic blend that brings nostalgia while expanding the audiences pallet. His intention is to ignite the yearning to explore and find something new in the age of comfort.
1-800-WHITTAKER is a local DJ & the owner of the NE Portland record store Music History.
For vinyl collector, DJ and radio host LAFLOR (Sabrina Cerquera), the artistry of DJing goes back to its most integral foundation–all the way to the roots.
A selector of vibes from all over the world, curating core memories for listeners wherever the music takes them.

DJ Lofi is a Portland, Oregon–based DJ, guitarist in the band Lowfires, and record collector with roots in Detroit. His taste leans toward the fringes—outsider folk, basement punk, private press oddities, and records that feel a little haunted.
Laura Peek is one of the most promising young Los Angeles–based stand-up comics to come out of Nashville's bustling comedy scene.
Raised on a steady diet of jungle and hardcore punk, she is known for her range and eclecticism.
Vinyl devotee and host of Manteca on KMHD, disco diablo spins genre-blurring sets full of thoughtful energy, and unexpected gems - all guided by a love of filling space with sound.
A club dad and longtime force in Portland’s underground, Andy has spent over a decade building bridges for dancers through his collective Believe You Me and his new home base, Process PDX.

Mintwhisper is a Portland-based DJ with roots in San Diego, influenced by the Bay Area and East Coast. Her selections move through deep house, disco, and soul, shaped by dubby textures and rhythm-forward energy.

Sean Jordan is a touring stand-up comedian and podcaster who has appeared on Comedy Central and The Late Late Show with James Corden, and whom Paste Magazine calls "both genuine and genuinely hilarious." He co-hosts the wildly popular podcast All Fantasy Everything, the show where funny people and…
Portland's Funniest Person of 2015 who started Pickathon comedy in 2016. She went on to a Comedy Central half-hour special, Last Comic Standing and CBS's After Midnight.
Katie Morris Henson is a Portland-based storyteller, speaker, and workshop facilitator, originally from a small town in East Texas.
Ron Turker started in the ’80s as a standup comic and medical student. Through a series of nonlinear events, he became a pediatric surgeon by day and an unrelenting writer by night.

Julia Corral is a Latina comic from Portland, OR, who's been described as the friendliest-caustic person you'll ever meet. The alt-weeklies have named her one of the Funniest 5 comics (Willamette Week) and an Undisputed Genius of Comedy (Portland Mercury).

A former winner of Portland's Funniest Person, you've probably seen Shain in projects for NBA 2K, Nike, Google, Lowe's, and Navy Federal Credit Union — and if not, he still got paid pretty well for all of them.

Kevin McGeehan is an award-winning storyteller, including 10 Moth StorySlams and the 2019 New York Moth GrandSlam Championship. He worked as an actor, writer, and teacher for Chicago’s famed Second City theater for over 20 years.
Terri Knight is an Oregon native and a fan favorite of Pants on Fire show. She has performed on the Mainstage with 7 Deadly Sins and is a featured teller on the “Backfence Unhinged” podcast.
Kevin Maloney is the author of Horse Girl Fever, The Red-Headed Pilgrim, and Cult of Loretta. His writing has appeared in Fence, HAD, Forever Magazine, and a number of other journals and anthologies.
Journalist and host of the Bundyville podcast. Her book Blazing Eye Sees All won the 2026 Oregon Book Award for General Nonfiction.

Rae Trotta (they/them) loves storytelling- they think it’s utter magic to be witnessed and to witness others. They tell stories around Portland including The Moth, BackFence, Mantis, Porch Hang, and more.

Dr. Mindy Nettifee is a poet, artist-educator, and somatic trauma therapist. She has published three full-length poetry collections and the how-to book on writing poetry Glitter in the Blood. Her latest collection is Open Your Mouth Like a Bell (Write Bloody).

Kaya Noteboom is a writer in Portland, OR. In 2025, she graduated from PNCA with a Master’s in Critical Studies. She now co-facilitates ACCESS CODE, a cultural criticism reading group, and hosts a monthly open mic for writers in or affected by recovery.

Frayn Masters is a performer, speaking / performance coach, producer, director, and writer. She is the creator and host of BACKFENCE Storytelling — including the BACKFENCE Unhinged podcast with co-host, Andrew Dickson.
Marissa Yang Bertucci is a writer, printmaker, and youth mental health worker. Marissa is a mixed Korean dyke, daughter of Yang Meehwa, and granddaughter of Yang Won-Dal and Lee Youngja.
First read at Pickathon as a debut novelist. The Edge of Water then won the Westport Prize and the Ploughshares Zacharis First Book Award and was named a TIME Best Book of the Year.
Beth Piatote is a Nez Perce scholar, playwright, poet, and associate professor of English and Comparative Literature at the University of California, Berkeley.
Read at Pickathon in 2018, before being named Oregon's 10th Poet Laureate in April 2020. He now curates Pickathon's poetry lineup.
Genevieve Hudson is the author of Boys of Alabama, which was a finalist for the Oregon Book Award, shortlisted for the Stonewall Book Award, and was named a Best Book of the Month by Apple Books.

Patti Wheeler is a writer and storyteller from Hell, Michigan. Her work centers on the importance of finding community and loving deeply. She recently sold her house in Detroit and bought a minivan and a historic home in the suburbs in the same month.

2024.l: Indie songwriters led. Jazz and hip-hop pushed in. Two favorites came back.
The band everyone was about to hear. Critics called them miraculous; that summer came Bonnaroo, Lollapalooza and Red Rocks.
A drummer and rapper working the seam between jazz and hip-hop, named by Mojo to its best albums of 2023.
Named one of the most exciting partnerships in music in 2023, Water From Your Eyes pushed indie into stranger shapes.

Grew up in Hillaryville, Louisiana, and formed the Indications while studying classical saxophone at Indiana University. His solo debut, Wait Til I Get Over, came out on Dead Oceans in 2023 and was reviewed by NPR, NME and Mojo.
A teenager from Winchester, Virginia who went viral in 2023, played the Grand Ole Opry at sixteen and signed to Atlantic.
A Burlington, Vermont DIY songwriter with a Stereogum SXSW showcase behind him. Burnover made Paste’s best of 2025.
An old-time fiddler who has toured with Willie Watson, with a debut solo album, Riveter, co-produced by Brittany Haas.
