2024.l: A New Orleans brass band that folds hip-hop and funk into second-line. They opened four Metallica anniversary shows at the Fillmore in 2011 and were the house band for the NFL Honors in 2013.
2024.sg: Culture in the Ghetto · Edge Sessions

2024.l: The Chicago band’s The Window took No. 1 on two year-end lists to end 2023 and made 21 ranked lists in all.
A Colorado band formed in 2006 that calls its style transcendental folk. It went on hiatus in 2018 and is back on the road.
Her self-released Appalachian record was reissued by Rounder, and she has played the Grand Ole Opry and Newport Folk.

2023.l: Two Asheville bands on the way up. Soul in the barns. A Sunday Haley Heynderickx saved.
Still playing small East Coast clubs that winter. A year later Manning Fireworks topped The New Yorker's list.
Her third Pickathon. She left home at 16 to tour and busk, and critics have kept coming back to her records ever since.
An East LA soul band on Colemine that grew into a full horn section. They come back in 2026.
2023.sg: Love Me Like You Used To · Edge Sessions

2023.l: Paste called the Paddock set maybe the best rock 'n' roll performance it saw all year. By December, Rat Saw God was its album of the year.
A couple from Victoria, B.C. That winter they sold out the Orpheum in Vancouver, the biggest show they'd ever played.
2023.sg: Like a River · On The Farm Sessions

2023.l: A Memphis bassist in head-to-toe neon who played with Prince. The Portland Mercury put his Galaxy Barn finale among its favorite moments of the weekend.
2023.sg: When I Am Weak I Am Strong · Edge Sessions

2023.l: A Korean-American country-blues singer and poet, signed to Dan Auerbach's Easy Eye Sound.
The band Zamrock is named around, out of Kitwe, Zambia. The Portland Mercury called the Woods set a masterclass.
A Birmingham trio, still Berklee students when they came. By 2025 they were opening at the Ryman and Telluride Bluegrass.
Chicago's alt-glam trio. Oregon ArtsWatch came away won over, mostly by Emily Kempf's voice.
Boston's traditional blues revival, with three albums in a row debuting at the top of the Billboard blues chart.
On Sunday COVID took Watchhouse off the bill. Haley said yes at the last minute and closed the Woods alone, with new songs.

story.t: Geese came back from their 2021 debut as a different band. Their album 3D Country was restless and unpredictable, and onstage they had turned volcanic.
more: Singer Cameron Winter wrote it around “modern doom,” the low hum of looming catastrophe, and wanted to meet it with irreverence instead of despair. Drummer Max Bassin called the result “like going to the circus and instead of having a good time, everyone is trying to kill you.”
Their bio said it plainly: this was not the band we thought they were, and no one could say where they would go next.

story.t: Three sets in three rooms. A Slab Session on Saturday at 6 p.m., a late-night Galaxy Barn set at 1 a.m., and Sunday night at 9 on the Woods stage.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024, a Discovery by 2025: already a critics’ favorite when they played Pickathon, then their own headline rooms jumped. Still climbing. They closed that summer supporting King Gizzard at Forest Hills Stadium, The Anthem, Red Rocks and the Gorge, then released Getting Killed in September 2025.
more: Getting Killed topped year-end lists at The New Yorker, NME and Stereogum and earned Pitchfork's Best New Music. Geese were the musical guest on Saturday Night Live in January 2026.
Their world tour mostly sold out theaters. On October 2, 2026 they headlined Forest Hills Stadium in Queens, their biggest headline show yet.

story.t: LA LOM started as the house band in the lobby of the Roosevelt Hotel in Hollywood, playing five nights a week. In June 2024 the guitar, bass and percussion trio signed to Verve Records and announced a debut album.
more: The group opened dates for Vampire Weekend that summer, and earlier in 2024 for Cory Wong. Its lead single, “Danza de LA LOM,” was a tribute to Peruvian cumbia and chicha.

story.t: Three sets: an Edge Session on Saturday evening, Cherry Hill after midnight that night, and the Woods stage on Sunday at 5 p.m. Their debut album came out five days later, on August 9.

Not yet a Discovery at Pickathon 2024, a Discovery by August 2025: they opened for Vampire Weekend the summer they played, then headlined The Wiltern in their hometown within a year. The debut opened at No. 5 on Billboard’s Tropical Albums chart, NPR reviewed it on August 19, 2024, and the band toured the U.S. and Europe that fall. They headlined The Wiltern on June 28, 2025, played Austin City Limits that October, and head into 2026 on tour with Thee Sacred Souls.

Nate Amos, who also plays in Water From Your Eyes, had been self-recording as This Is Lorelei for years. In June 2024 he released Box for Buddy, Box for Star on Double Double Whammy, an Album of the Week at Stereogum.
more: WXPN called it “the weirdest, but catchiest, alt-country album of the year.”
The record came out seven weeks before Pickathon. Pitchfork picked it as a best-of-the-week, and Paste gave it a strong review.

story.t: Three sets: Thursday at 11 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn, Friday at 2 p.m. in the Grove, and a late-night Edge Session after midnight that Friday.

Not yet a Discovery at Pickathon 2024, a Discovery by early 2026: a record critics loved in the summer of Pickathon led to a Matador deal and a headline tour. Along the way came tours with MJ Lenderman and Bleachers and festival dates at Primavera Sound and Roskilde in 2025. In March, Hayley Williams’s Power Snatch project covered “Perfect Hand,” and the fall headline tour ended at New York’s Webster Hall on November 6.

New Constellations is a Portland duo, Harlee Case and Josh Smith, friends since their teens in southern Oregon. By spring 2023 their first single, “Hot Blooded,” had more than 17 million streams and they were touring behind their debut EP.
more: “Hot Blooded” came out in January 2021 and got its video that September; the Lean In EP followed in 2023.

story.t: Four sets: Friday at 1 p.m. and Saturday at 9 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn, Sunday at noon in the Grove, and a Sunday 4:30 p.m. session in the Pumphouse. One writer covering the weekend said Portland’s New Constellations “seemed to be everywhere at this year’s Pickathon.”

Not yet a Discovery at Pickathon 2024, a Discovery by August 2025: a song that found millions of listeners turned into headline tours of their own through 2025. The Chicago Reader said the duo had “caught lightning in a bottle.” In 2026 they toured with The Midnight and released their debut album, It Comes in Waves, on May 15. Their own headline show at New York’s Bowery Ballroom was announced in September.

Water From Your Eyes is a New York duo, Rachel Brown and Nate Amos, who joined Matador Records in 2023 with Everyone’s Crushed. Pitchfork ranked that record No. 27 on its list of the best albums of 2023.
more: In April 2024, a few months before Pickathon, they opened for Interpol at a free show in Mexico City’s Zócalo, in front of a huge crowd.
Everyone’s Crushed was Pitchfork Best New Music and No. 36 on Rolling Stone’s best albums of 2023. They toured with Squid in February 2024 and Real Estate that May.

story.t: Three sets: a Slab Session at 2 p.m. and Cherry Hill at 7 p.m. on Thursday, then the Galaxy Barn at 7 p.m. on Friday. Pickathon listed them among that year’s emerging artists.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024, a Discovery by early 2026: critics’ darlings before Pickathon, they began selling out their own tours with It’s a Beautiful Place, released August 22, 2025. The fall headline tour was mostly sold out, including a sold-out London show.

Dean Johnson spent years tending bar at Al’s Tavern in Seattle’s Wallingford neighborhood, playing his own songs only now and then. He put out his first album, Nothing for Me, Please, on Mama Bird in May 2023, on his 50th birthday.
more: The Seattle Times called him “one of Seattle’s best kept secrets” that December. Pickathon named him a Rising Star Spotlight artist for 2024.
Paste gave the record a rave review and wrote that “Dean Johnson is no longer Seattle’s best-kept secret.”

story.t: Four sets: the Friday Curation dinner with Cameron Lee Dunlap of Morchella, the Woods on Saturday at 5 p.m., a Pumphouse Session on Sunday afternoon, and the Paddock on Sunday night.

Not yet a Discovery at Pickathon 2024, a Discovery by early 2026: signing to Saddle Creek in March 2025 turned a Seattle secret into a headliner across the country. His second album, I Hope We Can Still Be Friends, came out in August 2025, he toured with Rilo Kiley that September, and he headlined Portland’s Revolution Hall on November 20. This fall he is co-headlining a tour with Cat Clyde.

For three decades Will Oldham has made music as Bonnie “Prince” Billy on his own terms, prizing intimacy, community and mystery over the usual path. His 1999 album I See a Darkness became a touchstone, and Johnny Cash recorded its title song.
more: He came back to Pickathon in 2024, fourteen years after his first visit with The Cairo Gang, carrying Keeping Secrets Will Destroy You, a 2023 record made in Louisville with mostly local players.

story.t: Two nights, two very different rooms: Friday at 11 p.m. under the branches of the Woods, then Saturday at 10 p.m. on the Paddock, the main stage.

A Legend at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: three decades of records, and a draw that has not changed. Two new albums in barely a year. The Purple Bird arrived in January 2025 and We Are Together Again in March 2026, and critics met both warmly.
more: In October 2026 he and the Belgian quartet Linus announced The Outsider, a tribute album to the Dutch songwriter Jules de Corte.

story.t: Kara Jackson arrived as a poet first. The 2019 National Youth Poet Laureate from Oak Park, Illinois, turned that voice into Why Does the Earth Give Us People to Love?, a 2023 debut that landed on more than two dozen year-end lists.
more: The Line of Best Fit named it the No. 1 album of 2023. That spring she set out on her first headline tour, still playing small rooms.

story.t: Two sets in the trees: Friday afternoon at the Windmill, then Saturday at 6 p.m. in the Lucky Barn.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: one of the most praised albums of 2023, with her own rooms still the same size. Her voice keeps turning up in big company. She sings on Gorillaz’s “Orange County” from The Mountain (2026) and opens Moses Sumney’s soundtrack for the film IS GOD IS.
more: In 2025 she toured with Allison Russell and played Little Simz’s Meltdown festival at London’s Southbank Centre.

story.t: After more than a decade in Chicago, Ratboys left home for the first time to make The Window in Seattle with producer Chris Walla. Treble and Under the Radar both named it the No. 1 album of 2023.
more: It is soft-hearted Midwestern indie rock with a quiet Americana twist, from fuzzy power pop to fiddle-tinged country. Stereogum made it Album of the Week and Paste gave it a rave review.

story.t: Three sets, three rooms: a Pumphouse session Saturday afternoon, the Woods on Saturday at 7, and Cherry Hill on Sunday at 5.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024, a Discovery by August 2026. Ratboys signed with New West, and Singin’ to an Empty Chair (February 2026) won strong reviews from Pitchfork. They sold out Portland’s Aladdin Theater that spring and played NPR’s Tiny Desk in September.
more: In September 2026 a deluxe edition added covers of the album by Kevin Morby, PUP, Wild Pink and others.

story.t: Courtney Barnett first played Pickathon in 2014, two EPs into a career about to take off. Her 2015 debut, Sometimes I Sit and Think, and Sometimes I Just Sit, earned a Grammy nomination for Best New Artist.
more: She returned with End of the Day (2023), seventeen instrumental pieces first made as the score to the film Anonymous Club: a slow-burning turn from one of rock’s sharpest lyricists.
In 2014 she played the main stage on Sunday evening, then a packed Galaxy Barn set about an hour later.

story.t: Ten years after her first visit, she closed Sunday night on the Paddock, the main stage, at 10 p.m.

A Legend at Pickathon 2024 and still one now, back a decade after her first visit as a Discovery. Creature of Habit, her fourth album, came out in March 2026, written after a move from Melbourne to Los Angeles.
more: It is nominated for Best Rock Album at the 2026 ARIA Awards, and she spent 2026 touring theaters across North America and Australia.

story.t: Time Ain’t Accidental (2023) was the sound of a Texas-born songwriter running into her life head on: wide Western landscapes, tear-in-beer anthems and a modern country voice all her own.
more: It drew rave reviews and landed on more than a dozen 2023 year-end lists, high on Stereogum’s best country albums of the year.

story.t: Three sets, three rooms: the Woods on Friday at 5, a Pumphouse session Saturday morning, and Sunday evening in the Galaxy Barn.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: Time Ain’t Accidental landed on more than a dozen 2023 year-end lists, with no step up in her rooms since. A Mile South of Heaven, her sixth album, arrived in October 2026, produced by Shooter Jennings and her first on New West.
more: To mark it she adopted a two-mile stretch of Texas highway near Marfa.

story.t: Joanna Sternberg writes plain, open-hearted songs that land hard. Her 2023 album I’ve Got Me earned Best New Music and showed up on more than a dozen ranked year-end lists.
more: That spring she played Big Ears and Primavera Sound, still a songwriter most people were just finding.

story.t: Two sets in the trees: Friday at 1 p.m. on the Woods stage, then Saturday morning at the Windmill.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: I’ve Got Me made thirteen ranked 2023 year-end lists. Two weeks after Pickathon she released a new song, “A Country Dance.” She keeps sharing bills with songwriters she admires, including Stephin Merritt of The Magnetic Fields in 2026.
Portland’s Anna Tivel writes small, close-up stories about people at the edges. NPR Music named her album Outsiders among the best roots music of 2022 and gave her a Tiny Desk the next spring.
more: Living Thing, her sixth album, came out that May, written in lockdown while looking out the same window.

story.t: A home-state songwriter all over the farm: Thursday night at Cherry Hill, Sunday afternoon in the Lucky Barn, Sunday night on the Edge, and an On the Farm session of “Two Truths.”

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and a surer one by early 2025: NPR named Outsiders the best roots music of 2022 and gave her a Tiny Desk. Living Thing was named Folk Alley’s No. 1 album of 2024. Animal Poem followed in August 2025, and in March 2026 she made her Big Ears debut.

Irreversible Entanglements, the free-jazz collective led by poet Camae Ayewa (Moor Mother), arrived on Impulse! with Protect Your Light, a 2023 record jazz critics put at or near the top of their lists.
more: In February 2024 they played an NPR Tiny Desk concert, six songs straight through with no breaks.

story.t: Saturday afternoon in the Galaxy Barn, then Sunday at 3 on the Woods stage. One festival reviewer wrote that two incendiary sets were hardly enough.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: Protect Your Light and a Tiny Desk in February 2024 kept jazz critics’ attention, but no bigger rooms have shown up. Future Present Past, their fifth album, came out on Impulse! in March 2026, recorded at Van Gelder Studio, and critics met it warmly.
more: They took it on the road across Europe that spring.

story.t: Chicago rapper McKinley Dixon built Beloved! Paradise! Jazz!? out of live jazz and hard-won storytelling. Critics ranked it among 2023’s best, No. 3 at Paste and No. 7 at Consequence.
Pickathon named him one of the year’s breakout stars. He played the Galaxy Barn at 11 on Saturday night and Cherry Hill at 7 on Sunday.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: Beloved! Paradise! Jazz!? was No. 3 on Paste’s 2023 list. Magic, Alive! arrived in June 2025 and landed at No. 2 on The Independent’s best albums of the year.
more: He toured it across the US and Europe that fall.

story.t: The Soul Rebels have carried New Orleans brass into hip-hop, funk and soul since 1991, from Tipitina’s to Bonnaroo, the Montreal Jazz Festival and four nights opening for Metallica.
more: In the spring of 2024 they played Jazz Fest, the Hollywood Bowl and three nights at the Blue Note in New York with Wu-Tang Clan’s GZA and Ghostface Killah.

story.t: Four sets in three days: Saturday night in the Woods, a 1 a.m. set on the Edge, Sunday brunch at the Curation table with Rodney Muirhead of Podnah’s Pit, and the midnight close on the Paddock. Their Woods set turned the trees into a New Orleans party.

A Legend at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: founded in New Orleans in 1991, with Bonnaroo, Montreal Jazz Fest and four Metallica openers behind them. They played the Super Bowl LIX pregame in New Orleans in February 2025.
more: In October 2026 they recorded new anthems in Paris for the Saints and Paris Saint-Germain.

story.t: Elephant Revival is a Colorado folk band led by the voice of Bonnie Paine, mixing Celtic, string-band and indie folk into something meditative. They headlined Red Rocks, said goodbye there on May 20, 2018, and reunited in 2022.
more: Their last album before the break was Petals (2016). Relix called it “more confident and assured than ever.”

story.t: Four appearances: the Paddock on Friday at 10 p.m., a Saturday Curation dinner with chef Luna Contreras of Chelo, the Edge on Saturday at 11 p.m., and the Woods on Sunday at 11 p.m.

A Legend at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: a Colorado folk institution that closed Red Rocks and came back on its own terms. They headlined Denver’s Mission Ballroom on April 11, 2025, and this fall played Belly Up Aspen and Dillon Amphitheater.

Fust is a Durham, North Carolina alt-country band led by songwriter Aaron Dowdy. Their album Genevieve (Dear Life, 2023) made two Pitchfork lists that year: new albums to listen to now, and great records you may have missed.
Three sets: the Windmill on Thursday at 3 p.m., a Slab session at 6:30 that evening, and the Grove on Friday at noon.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now. Big Ugly (March 7, 2025) landed on best-of-2025 lists at Time and Paste, and NPR named “Spangled” one of its 25 best songs of the year, though they still play club rooms. They played songs from it on CBS Saturday Morning and kept touring into 2026.

Searows is Alec Duckart, a Portland songwriter making hushed, intimate folk in the line of Phoebe Bridgers and Bon Iver. After the self-released Guard Dog (late 2022) and the End of the World EP, Paste named him a Best of What’s Next artist in December 2023.
more: He opened Gracie Abrams’s first European tour and has toured with Matt Maltese.

story.t: Three sets: a Pumphouse session on Friday at 1:30 p.m., Cherry Hill that evening at 7, and the Grove on Sunday at 2 p.m. Pickathon had named him one of its possible breakout stars that June.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024, a Discovery by 2025: a Portland songwriter who opened for others came back with a new record and headline tours of his own on two continents. He toured with Tamino in October 2025, released Death in the Business of Whaling on January 23, 2026, and headlined New York’s Webster Hall on May 6. His first Australian tour is set for November.

Rogê is a Rio de Janeiro songwriter from the Lapa scene, making warm retro samba-funk in the line of Jorge Ben and Gilberto Gil. His album Curyman (Diamond West, May 2023) was produced by Thomas Brenneck, with strings by Arthur Verocai, and drew a strong review from Songlines.
more: In August 2022 he sat in with the Gipsy Kings at the Hollywood Bowl.

story.t: Three sets: the Woods on Saturday at 1 p.m., the Edge at 9 p.m., and the Paddock after midnight. Covering the weekend for VRTX, Ryan J. Prado wrote that he “brought a resounding message of resilience and samba energy to the Woods Stage.”

A Legend at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: a star of Rio’s samba scene for more than two decades, newly carried abroad by Curyman. Curyman II followed in November 2024, and he took it to New York’s Public Theater and the Holland Festival.

Billie Marten is a Yorkshire songwriter making hushed, intimate folk, and she has been releasing records since 2016. Drop Cherries (Fiction, April 2023) drew rave reviews and took No. 5 on The Independent’s best albums of 2023.
more: The Independent gave Drop Cherries a rave review.

story.t: Four appearances: a Saturday Curation brunch with chefs Lauren Breneman and John Boisse of Astral PDX, a 3 p.m. set that afternoon, Cherry Hill that evening at 7, and the Woods on Sunday at 7 p.m.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now. Dog Eared (July 2025, her fifth album) drew rave reviews and went to No. 1 on the UK folk albums chart. She opened for Tennis in the US and played UK dates with Elbow, headlined London’s O2 Forum Kentish Town on November 15, 2025, and took the record to Australia and New Zealand in February.

Kassa Overall is a Brooklyn drummer, producer and rapper who bends jazz and hip-hop together. Animals (Warp, May 2023) went to No. 1 on KEXP’s chart the week it came out and made Mojo’s best albums of 2023, and he played his second NPR Tiny Desk that April.
Three sets: the Paddock on Thursday at 8 p.m., a Slab session on Friday at 1:30, and the Galaxy Barn that night at 9.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now. CREAM (Warp, September 12, 2025) reworks hip-hop classics as jazz and turned up on 21 year-end lists. He won a 2025 Doris Duke Artist Award and was on the bill at Nice Jazz Festival in 2026.

Melissa Carper is an upright bassist and singer from Austin, by way of Nebraska and Arkansas, with years in the Carper Family and Sad Daddy behind her. Daddy’s Country Gold (Free Dirt, 2021) was nominated for Saving Country Music’s 2021 Album of the Year, and Rolling Stone named her 2022 record Ramblin’ Soul one of the year’s best country albums.
Three sets: the Woods on Friday at 11 a.m., a second Friday set at 6 p.m., and the Galaxy Barn on Saturday at 7 p.m.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now. Borned in Ya (Thirty Tigers, 2024) landed at No. 7 on Folk Alley’s best albums of the year. In December 2025 she opened every date of JD McPherson’s tour, ending at First Avenue in Minneapolis, and on February 6, 2026 she and fellow Pickathon 2024 act Theo Lawrence released the duet album Havin’ a Talk on Warner Records.

Adi Oasis is a singer and bassist raised outside Paris and based in Brooklyn, playing neo-soul and funk with real low end. Her second album, Lotus Glow (March 2023), was a Bandcamp Daily Album of the Day. She played North Sea Jazz and Nice Jazz Fest that year, then headlined La Cigale in Paris on April 24, 2024, a few months before the Portland Mercury named her one of nine Pickathon picks.
more: She has toured with Anderson .Paak and played bass in CeeLo Green’s band.

story.t: Two sets: the Galaxy Barn on Thursday at 9 p.m. and Cherry Hill on Friday at 11 p.m.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: a bassist-singer who keeps working jazz festivals and clubs around the world rather than climbing past them. She played Blue Note São Paulo in November 2024 and has kept up festival dates in Europe and the US since.
Greg Freeman is a Vermont songwriter making alt-country and indie rock with pedal steel and big hooks. His debut, I Looked Out (Bud Tapes, 2022), came out two years before he played Pickathon.
Three sets: the Slab on Friday at noon, the Paddock that night at 8, and Cherry Hill on Sunday at 11 p.m.

Not yet a Discovery at Pickathon 2024, a Discovery by late 2026: a small-room support act who made one of 2025’s most praised rock records and now headlines on his own. I Looked Out was reissued in November 2024 on Canvasback and Transgressive, and Burnover (August 22, 2025) drew a rave from Paste, which called him “a rock hero in the making” and ranked it No. 47 of 2025. This month he headlined Portland’s Aladdin Theater, and a new album, All Set the Bone, is announced.

Vincent Neil Emerson is a Texas songwriter in the outlaw country tradition, with records produced over the years by Rodney Crowell, Shooter Jennings and Patrick Lyons. The Golden Crystal Kingdom (2023, produced by Shooter Jennings) was the record behind his booking, and his songs have been placed in Reservation Dogs, Yellowstone and Landman.

Three sets: an afternoon set on Friday at 3, Cherry Hill that night at 9, and a late set on the Woods on Saturday night that was not on the printed schedule. He also sat down for an episode of the Pickathon Podcast.

Not yet a Discovery at Pickathon 2024, a Discovery by early 2026, though not a certain one, because his earlier rooms were already similar. In 2025 he began headlining on his own, including New York’s Bowery Ballroom on August 15. Blue Stars (April 2026, produced by Patrick Lyons) earned a strong review from Saving Country Music, and the tour behind it included two nights at Denver’s Bluebird Theater.

Bella White is a Nova Scotia-born singer-songwriter who blends bluegrass and Appalachian folk with modern Americana, and Rolling Stone called her songwriting “sublime Appalachian heartbreak” in 2020. Among Other Things (Rounder, 2023) arrived the year she made her Grand Ole Opry debut, played Newport Folk and Stagecoach, and had “Burn Me Once” on the soundtrack of The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes.
She first played Pickathon in 2022 and came back for three sets in 2024: the Paddock on Friday at 6 p.m., the Woods on Saturday at 11 a.m., and the Pumphouse that afternoon at 3.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024, a Discovery by fall 2026: she went from a Rounder-label favorite to headlining her own fall tour, including Denver’s Gothic Theatre on October 23. A Sign in the Weather, her third album, came out this year and Saving Country Music gave it a strong review.

Rhododendron is a young Portland trio that mixes 1980s and 1990s underground rock with jazz, ambient and progressive touches; they formed in 2019 as School of Rock students. Protozoan Battle Hymns (2021) was their record at booking, and Willamette Week featured them in February 2024 as part of Portland’s youth rock scene.
more: The Portland Mercury put them on its list of nine Pickathon sets not to miss.

story.t: Three sets: a Slab session on Thursday at 3:30, the Galaxy Barn on Saturday at 5, and the Windmill on Sunday at 1. At the Windmill, VRTX heard “electric technicality anchored a raucous set of post-rock mayhem.”

Not yet a Discovery at Pickathon 2024, a Discovery by August 2026, though not a certain one, with no streaming or press ranks yet behind it. A young Portland band signed to The Flenser (announced March 3, 2026), the label of Chat Pile and Have A Nice Life, released Ascent Effort there on May 15, and headlined Portland’s Aladdin Theater on May 30.

Theo Lawrence is a Bordeaux-born country-soul singer who leads The Hearts. Paris knew him first: Fnac named his debut album its pick of the month in March 2018, and his show at La Maroquinerie sold out in January 2020. Cherie followed in 2023.

Three sets: Cherry Hill on Friday at 5 p.m., the Edge that night at 11, and the Paddock on Saturday at 6. VRTX called the band’s sets “timewarp country sets straight out of the AM radio salad days,” and at the Paddock Glide heard “I’m Working on a Building” get the crowd dancing, then the dreamy western ballad “Prairie Fire” and the waltz “Hill of Love.”

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: a Warner Records deal and a long run opening for Alison Krauss could tip him toward Discovery once his own rooms grow. He released a duet single with Melissa Carper in January 2025, and their duets album Havin’ A Talk came out February 6, 2026. In April 2026 he made his national TV debut on CBS Saturday Morning, and he is opening for Alison Krauss & Union Station from April to October, ahead of a debut full-length on Warner and Reprise.

Durand Jones is the singer and saxophonist who fronts Durand Jones & The Indications, a soul band from Bloomington, Indiana, with Dead Oceans albums through 2021. He came to Pickathon off Wait Til I Get Over (May 2023), his first solo album, which drew rave reviews, NME’s among them.
more: The Indications’ Private Space (2021) reached No. 127 on the Billboard 200, and the band drew Libera Award nominations in 2019 and 2020.

story.t: Three sets: an afternoon set on Thursday at 4:30, the Paddock that night at 10, and the Woods on Friday at 7. Eleven PDX’s preview called him “a modern soul revivalist.”

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: the theater rooms of his 2025 tour were a level the band had already reached before Pickathon, so there has been no step up. Flowers (Dead Oceans, June 27, 2025), the Indications’ first album since 2021, led a fall tour that reached Los Angeles’ Greek Theatre, Chicago’s Salt Shed and the Fox Theater in Oakland.

Jeffrey Martin is a folk songwriter whose plainspoken, deeply felt songs have drawn comparisons to John Prine and John Moreland. He wrote his 2023 album Thank God We Left the Garden over a winter in a tiny backyard shack in southeast Portland, and the demos from that shack became the record itself. Pickathon named him one of its 2024 Breakout Stars.
He played the Lucky Barn on Friday at 6 p.m. and the Windmill on Sunday at 3, with a Thursday afternoon set at the Pumphouse as well.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now. He headlined Minneapolis’s 7th St Entry in May 2024, then toured Ireland and the UK in early 2026, including Dublin’s Whelan’s on January 29. Alive July 25, 2025, a live album recorded at Portland’s Showdown and led by a Neil Young cover, came out February 20, 2026, and in March he made his Australian debut, with dates at Port Fairy Folk Festival and the Blue Mountains Music Festival.

Pahua is Paulina Sotomayor, a composer, percussionist, DJ and producer from Mexico City who started out as a mariachi singer at age six. Her music bridges folklore and electronics, mixing Latin American rhythms such as cumbia and dembow with marimbas and drums. Habita (2023), her first full-length, came together with a dozen collaborators, and KEXP’s El Sonido featured her in July 2023. Rolling Stone en Español profiled her in May 2024, and the Portland Mercury put her on its list of nine Pickathon sets not to miss.

Four appearances: a Saturday-afternoon cooking session at Curation, Cherry Hill on Saturday night at 9, a Pumphouse set on Sunday at 3, and a Galaxy Barn set after midnight that night, at 1 a.m. Sunday.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now, though not a certain one: she remains a favorite of world-music and club-night crowds without a clear jump in her own rooms. She also reunited with her brother Raúl as Sotomayor, releasing “Who’s There” as the duo’s lead single.

Ellis Bullard is an Austin honky-tonk singer who leads a band called Jake & The Hill People. His mother sang in the Muscle Shoals studios in the 1960s and ‘70s. Piss-Hot Freightlining Country Music (2022) and then Honky Tonk Ain’t Noise Pollution (Feel So Good Records, February 9, 2024) each earned a strong review from Saving Country Music, and Joe Rogan has praised the band on his podcast.

Three sets: the Edge on Friday at 9 p.m., the Galaxy Barn at 1 a.m. that night, and Cherry Hill on Sunday at 9. He also played Portland’s Showdown Saloon on Saturday, August 3, as part of its Pickathon week.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now, with a growing case for Discovery as his own headline dates get bigger. Saving Country Music named Honky Tonk Ain’t Noise Pollution one of its Essential Albums of 2024, Rolling Stone Country ran a feature on him in 2025, and on May 1, 2026 he headlined Cowboys & Cadillacs, with club and dance-hall dates through the summer.

Erin Rae is a Nashville singer-songwriter with a hushed, indie-folk voice. Putting On Airs (2018) earned her an Emerging Act nomination at the 2019 Americana Music Awards, Lighten Up (2022) drew a strong Mojo review, and in 2023 she won Newport Folk’s Jim James Award for the most sit-ins. Her voice was on Tyler Childers’ Rustin’ in the Rain that September.
Three sets: Cherry Hill after midnight on Friday, a Saturday-afternoon set at 1:30, and the Lucky Barn on Saturday at 4.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: still a critics’ and songwriters’ favorite, with the Americana world behind her and no step up in her own headline rooms yet. She released the singles “Early Blue” and “On Her Side” and the Lagniappe Session EP in 2024, and she is booked for Wales’ Boia Festival in St Davids, October 23 to 25, 2026.

True Loves is a Seattle funk and soul band that formed in 2014 after a jam session, known for tight grooves, a big horn section and matching outfits. KEXP’s John Richards once called them “the best dressed band in the city,” and their 2018 KEXP session has passed two million YouTube views. Sunday Afternoon (2021) was their record when Pickathon booked them.
Three sets in two days: the Edge on Thursday at 7 p.m., Cherry Hill that night at 11, and the Galaxy Barn on Friday at 5.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now, though not a certain one: Seattle’s best-loved live band, still without a step up in rooms beyond their home region. A funky new single, “Good Weed and Red Wine,” came out that August, their first release since Sunday Afternoon, followed by a fall European tour. They are back in Europe this November, with shows in the Netherlands and Zurich’s Moods on November 16.

Daniel Villarreal is a drummer and composer born in Panama City who moved to the United States in the early 2000s and now lives in Philadelphia. His 2022 debut as a leader, Panamá 77, came out on International Anthem and landed on a run of jazz-press year-end lists; MOJO heard cumbia, chicha, folk, reggaeton and salsa folded into the jazz. A second album, Lados B, followed in 2023.
Three sets: the Edge on Friday at 7 p.m., the Paddock after midnight that night, and the Galaxy Barn on Sunday at 9.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now. He played Minneapolis’s Cedar summer series, and in July 2026 he made his SFJAZZ debut with two nights in the Joe Henderson Lab, playing a new trio set built around his 2026 debut album with that group.

Florry is a country-leaning indie rock band led by Francie Medosch, with a twangy sound that draws on The Band and Silver Jews. Their 2023 album The Holey Bible was Stereogum’s Album of the Week and made BrooklynVegan’s list of the year’s best country records.
Three sets: the Paddock on Saturday at 8 p.m., the Grove on Sunday at 4, and the Edge after midnight on Saturday night.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now. Sounds Like…, produced by Colin Miller, came out May 23, 2025 on Dear Life Records, with “Hey Baby” as the first single and a June tour from Burlington, Vermont to Medford, Massachusetts. In 2026 they are co-headlining club dates with Friendship, including Spokane’s Chameleon on July 29.

Jake Kohn grew up in Stephens City, Virginia. A video of him singing “Hard As Stone” for Radio WV went viral early in 2023, when he was 15, and by September he had made his Grand Ole Opry debut. His first single, “Frostbite,” came out on Atlantic that November.
Three sets: the Lucky Barn on Friday at noon, the Pumphouse on Friday at 3, and the Grove on Saturday at noon.

He played Newport Folk on July 28, 2024 and Bourbon & Beyond that September. His debut album, Where Do We Go From Here?, arrived June 27, 2025, with another Opry date that July, and he headlined clubs that fall.

Mitchum Yacoub is a San Diego percussionist and bandleader whose music runs on Afro-Latin percussion, horn lines and long, repeating grooves in the soul, funk and Afrobeat tradition. His debut album, Living High in the Brass Empire, came out on All-Town Sound on June 30, 2023.
Three sets: the Galaxy Barn after midnight on Thursday, the Slab on Friday at 4:30, and the Woods on Friday at 9 p.m.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: a favorite of the Afro-Latin dance floor, still playing mid-size rooms. In 2026 he has been touring as a co-bill with the Los Angeles Afro-Latin funk band Jungle Fire, including Bend’s Tower Theatre on March 15.

Sluice is a North Carolina band that began as Justin Morris’s songwriting project in Durham, with a lineup that has grown to a four-piece. Its second album, Radial Gate (2023), is about isolation and depression giving way to community, and it made the Guardian’s best-of-2023-so-far list that June. The band played Hopscotch that fall.
Three sets: the Grove on Saturday at 2 p.m., the Pumphouse that afternoon at 4:30, and the Woods on Sunday at 1.
A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now. Companion, the third album and the first on Mtn Laurel Recording Co., came out March 27, 2026, led by the single “Beadie.”

Two Runner is Paige Anderson and Emilie Rose, who grew up in Nevada City, California and began playing together in 2020. Anderson is a multi-instrumentalist who toured for a decade with her family band, and Rose is a Berklee-trained fiddler. They call their sound Americana-folk-roots-old time-bluegrass, with close harmony and a rougher edge. Their self-produced debut, Modern Cowboy, came out in 2023, a year of steady touring.
Three sets: the Lucky Barn on Friday at 4 p.m., a Saturday-noon set, and the Windmill on Saturday at 3.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: a duo that earns its crowds one festival and club at a time, with no step up we could find. They played Colorado’s RockyGrass days before Pickathon, and their 2026 dates include club rooms such as Jammin Java in Virginia and Whelan’s in Dublin.

Sami Braman is a fiddler who grew up in Seattle and is now based in Nashville. She plays in the old-time band The Onlies and has played with Willie Watson of Old Crow Medicine Show. Riveter, her debut album of original fiddle tunes, came out on Padiddle Records on April 7, 2023, and she headlined New York’s Jalopy Theatre that month.
Four slots: a Thursday-afternoon set at 1:30, the Squaredance she called on the Paddock that evening at 6, the Woods on Friday at 3, and the Lucky Barn on Saturday at 2.
A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now. Her Riveter tunes remain the calling card, and she keeps playing with The Onlies.

JD Simo is a guitarist, singer and producer born in Chicago and based in Nashville. He fronted the psychedelic blues-rock band SIMO from 2012 to 2018, and he is credited with playing all the live guitar in Baz Luhrmann’s Elvis film. His 2023 album Songs From the House of Grease came out that January, and he was special guest on the Allman Betts Band’s December run.
Three sets: Cherry Hill on Saturday at 11 p.m., the Paddock on Sunday at 6, and the Edge on Sunday at 11 p.m.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: a guitarist’s guitarist whose name is bigger among players than in his own headline rooms. He was special guest at San Francisco’s Fillmore that August, and that fall he released Do The Rump, an album with Luther Dickinson and Adam Abrashoff.

John Haywood is an old-time banjo player from Letcher County, Kentucky, who learned from the banjo master George Gibson and played with the late Lee Sexton’s band. He is also a tattoo artist who opened Parlor Room Art and Tattoo in Whitesburg in 2011. His banjo is on Tyler Childers’ Long Violent History, a Grammy-nominated album, and he has played with Childers at Radio City Music Hall, Bonnaroo and Red Rocks.
Four sets: a Thursday-noon set, the Grove on Thursday at 4, the Edge after midnight that night, and the Lucky Barn on Friday at 2.

A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: a banjo player the old-time world reveres, whose fame still runs through Childers’ stage rather than his own. He is on the faculty at Kentucky’s Cowan Creek Music Gathering and has released a solo banjo record, Upon My Word Honor.

Will Paquin is a guitarist whose fingerstyle covers took off on TikTok in 2020, when he was a student at Boston University. His own songs are fingerpicked, intimate pop. He headlined Los Angeles’s Moroccan Lounge in August 2023, a year before Pickathon.
Three sets: the Windmill on Thursday at 1 p.m., the Pumphouse on Friday at noon, and the Galaxy Barn on Sunday at 1.

Not yet a Deep cut at Pickathon 2024, a Deep cut by early 2026: a TikTok-born guitarist who had played little live, then made a record and a festival run. Hahaha, his first album, came out September 12, 2025, with a North American headline tour, and that November he played a Pitchfork festival slot and Live at Leeds.

PACKS is the Toronto indie-rock project of Madeline Link, a band since 2019 with Shane Hooper, Dexter Nash and Noah O’Neil. They signed to Fire Talk in 2020 and made Take the Cake (2021) and Crispy Crunchy Nothing (2023, partly recorded in a rural Quebec cabin). Melt the Honey came out January 19, 2024, six months before Pickathon, and drew good reviews.
Three sets: the Slab on Saturday at 3 p.m., Cherry Hill at 5, and the Galaxy Barn on Sunday at 7.
A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now, a medium-confidence call. Their next single, “before i was bleeding,” arrived in February 2025.

JJUUJJUU is a Los Angeles experimental psychedelic collective fronted by Phil Pirrone, who co-founded the Desert Daze festival. They released “Some” with Brazil’s Boogarins in January 2024 and played both weekends of Coachella that April, then put out “Up To You.”

Three sets: the Slab on Saturday at 1:30, the Grove at 4, and a late one in the Galaxy Barn on Sunday at 11 p.m. Pickathon was one stop on a summer that also took them to Electric Forest, Green Man and Freakout Fest.
A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now, a medium-confidence call: a festival act with real standing in the psychedelic world, and no step into larger rooms since.

Lo Steele is a Portland neo-soul singer-songwriter and the daughter of LaRhonda Steele, the “First Lady of Portland Blues.” Her first full-length, Happy Girl, came out June 30, 2023, and she had already played the Waterfront Blues Festival.
Three sets: Cherry Hill on Thursday at 5 p.m., the Edge that night at 11, and the Windmill on Friday at 11 a.m.
A Deep cut at Pickathon 2024 and still one now: a Portland voice with deep local roots who has built slowly. She won two Drammy Awards and released a new album, Only a Drop, in March 2026.
The Macks are a Portland band fronted by vocalist Sam Fulwiler, named Best New Band by Willamette Week in 2022.
Three sets: the Slab on Friday at 3 p.m., the Galaxy Barn that night at 11, and the Windmill on Saturday at 1.

Not yet a Deep cut at Pickathon 2024, a Deep cut by early 2026: a local favorite that grew into a touring band. Bonanza came out September 25, 2025, on DevilDuck and Monotone in the US and Glitterhouse in Europe, followed by a fall tour with Acid Mothers Temple, and they are booked for Treefort 2027.
Color Green is a Los Angeles psych-rock and cosmic-country band built around bassist-vocalist Kyla Perlmutter and four vocalists. Their harmonies are the draw.
Three sets: the Edge on Thursday at 9 p.m., the Paddock after midnight that night, and the Grove on Friday at 4.

Neither at Pickathon 2024 and still Neither: a band with a devoted following and no step up we could find. Weeks after Pickathon they announced Fool’s Parade, nine songs produced by Mike Kriebel for New West Records.

foamboy is the Portland duo of Katy Ohsiek and Wil Bakula, who began as a remote recording collaboration and now play live with five more musicians. Their debut, My Sober Daydream, came out in 2021. Willamette Week profiled them among Portland’s Best New Bands, and their second album, Eating Me Alive, came out March 8, 2024, five months before Pickathon.
Three sets: the Lucky Barn on Saturday at noon, the Pumphouse on Sunday at noon, and the Galaxy Barn on Sunday at 3.

Neither at Pickathon 2024 and still Neither, a medium-confidence call and a close second to a Deep cut: a well-liked Portland band that has stayed close to home, with no outside list, review or larger room we could find. Eating Me Alive got a deluxe edition with six B-sides.

Johnny Franco performs with his real brother Dom. They moved to Portland from São Paulo, and they play jangly, Brazilian-tinged rock and roll with a showman’s sense of humor. Johnny is signed to Blanket Fort, the label run by producer Sterling Fox, and put out the EP Experience Report #1. Their own Portland shows had sold out the Doug Fir twice.
Five sets: the Galaxy Barn on Friday at 3 p.m., the Slab at 6, the Woods on Saturday at 3, the Lucky Barn on Sunday at 2, and the Edge that night at 7.

Neither at Pickathon 2024 and still Neither, a medium-confidence call and a close second to a Deep cut: a cult act at home with no outside validation that we could find. They still play Portland rooms and park concerts.

Logan Halstead was born in Kentucky and raised in West Virginia. A video of him playing the title song for Radio West Virginia went viral, and he sang on Arlo McKinley’s “Back Home.” His debut album, Dark Black Coal, came out May 5, 2023 on Thirty Tigers, produced by Lawrence Rothman, when he was 19.
Four sets: the Windmill on Friday at 1 p.m., the Pumphouse at 5, the Galaxy Barn on Saturday at 1, and one more Saturday at 4:30.
Neither at Pickathon 2024 and still Neither, a medium-confidence call and a close second to a Discovery: a young songwriter with a major-label-adjacent debut and real fans. We found no step up since.

The Barbaras are sisters Weezy and Sallie Ford, who write Portland songs out of mid-century country, doo-wop and rock ’n’ roll with a modern lyrical eye. Their debut album, Oh My God Barbara, came out in 2022, with a band that includes James Greenan, Jeff Munger and Mark Robertson.
Three sets: the Grove on Thursday at 2 p.m., another Thursday set at 6, and the Lucky Barn on Sunday at 6.

Neither at Pickathon 2024 and still Neither, a medium-confidence call and a close second to a Deep cut: a Portland band that fills local bills and press picks, with no outside list or larger room we could find. Pickathon’s own shows do not count as outside evidence.

That February Jake Lenderman was still playing small clubs on the East Coast, and in July he signed with Anti-. Boat Songs had already landed on a few year-end lists, so he came to the farm rising, not unknown.
more: When the lineup came out, Stereogum pulled two names off the bill: his and Wednesday's.

story.t: Three sets: Friday at noon on the Slab, Friday at 3 p.m. in the Woods and Sunday at 5 p.m. at Cherry Hill.
Manning Fireworks came out the next September. Pitchfork gave it Best New Music, and it ended up on 69 year-end lists, number one at The New Yorker.
more: In April 2025 he sold out three nights in a row at Brooklyn Steel, and that August he headlined the Roundhouse in London. Lately he's been in Snocaps and singing backup on Mavis Staples' Sad and Beautiful World.

story.t: Rat Saw God came out on Dead Oceans in April 2023, four months before the festival. The spring tour behind it was still clubs: The Earl, Mississippi Studios, Fox Cabaret.
more: Karly Hartzman writes songs we described as quilts of the American South, and they'd just played Primavera Sound.

story.t: Three sets: Saturday at 5:15 p.m. on the Slab, Saturday at 8 p.m. at the Paddock and Sunday at 9 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn.
By December Rat Saw God was album of the year at Paste and Stereogum, and number 4 at Pitchfork.
more: In January 2024 they headlined a sold-out Brooklyn Steel. Bleeds followed in September 2025, and they played Colbert that May.

story.t: She left home at 16 to tour and busk, and by 2023 she had a decade of records critics kept coming back to. Honest Life topped the UK Americana chart, and she was named International Artist of the Year at the 2018 UK Americana Awards.
more: May Your Kindness Remain made The Guardian's best albums of 2018, and Old Flowers drew New York Times praise in 2020.

story.t: Two sets: Friday at 9 p.m. at Cherry Hill and Saturday at 6 p.m. in the Grove. Her third Pickathon, six years after her first.
A Deep cut in 2017 and a Deep cut again in 2023.
more: Loose Future came out on Fat Possum in 2022, produced by Sam Evian.

story.t: Lee Fields cut his first single in 1969, when people called him Little JB. By 2023 he was on Daptone, with Sentimental Fool out the year before, and his song "Forever" had just run in a Super Bowl ad.
more: Willamette Week called him a soul legend in its lineup story.

story.t: Two sets: Friday at 9 p.m. in the Woods and Saturday at 9 p.m. at Cherry Hill. His second Pickathon, twelve years after the first. Oregon ArtsWatch made him a favorite of the weekend for the energy and the voice of a 73-year-old.
A Discovery in 2011, two years after My World helped set off the retro-soul revival, and a Legend by 2023: a career that started in 1969 and never stopped.
more: The documentary Lee Fields: Faithful Man came out in 2024, and in 2025 he joined the Alabama Shakes reunion tour as a special guest.

story.t: A Birmingham bluegrass trio, and two of them were still Berklee students. Hardly anyone outside Alabama knew them yet.
Three sets: Saturday at 5 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn, Sunday at 6 p.m. in the Grove and 1 a.m. Sunday night at the Edge.
They played DelFest and WinterWonderGrass in 2024, and in 2025 they opened at Telluride Bluegrass and at the Ryman.
more: They were still touring in a little white van and taking opening slots, and building their own headline rooms.

story.t: A Nigerian-Canadian rapper and singer who'd won the 2021 Juno for Rap Recording of the Year and been shortlisted for the Polaris Prize the same year.
more: His music turned up in HBO's Insecure back in 2017.

story.t: Three sets: Thursday at 7 p.m. at the Edge, 1 a.m. Thursday night in the Galaxy Barn and Friday at 5 p.m. in the Woods.
He came with one Juno and one Polaris shortlist. Everything since doubled it: two more Junos in 2024, for PANIC and the single "Someone I Knew," and a second Polaris shortlist for PANIC.
The band Zamrock is named around. W.I.T.C.H. came out of Kitwe, Zambia, in 1972 and were the biggest band in the country for most of that decade.
more: Reissues brought them back, Now-Again's We Intend to Cause Havoc! in 2011 among them, and Emanyeo "Jagari" Chanda revived the band in 2012. Zango, their first studio album in nearly forty years, came out in 2023.

story.t: Three sets: Saturday at 7 p.m. in the Woods, Saturday at 11 p.m. at the Edge and Sunday at 10 p.m. at the Paddock. The Portland Mercury called the Woods set a masterclass, the kind that wins fans for life.
A Legend then and now: already a legend in their world in 1975, and rediscovered twice since.
more: Sogolo came out in June 2025.

story.t: Andrew Marlin and Emily Frantz started playing together in 2009 as Mandolin Orange, and in 2021 they renamed the band Watchhouse.
more: In 2022 they toured with Punch Brothers on the American Acoustic run.

story.t: One set: Saturday at 11 p.m. at Cherry Hill. COVID took their Sunday, and Haley Heynderickx closed the Woods in their place.
The same two people, a new name and a decade between: a Discovery in 2014 as Mandolin Orange, a Legend by 2023.
more: Andrew Marlin's first Grammy nomination came the next winter, Best Bluegrass Album for Mighty Poplar.

story.t: A Portland songwriter who first played the farm in 2018.

One set: Sunday at 9 p.m. in the Woods. COVID knocked out Watchhouse, and she said yes at the last minute. Five years after her first Pickathon she had the Woods to herself, with a set of new songs Oregon ArtsWatch called intimate.
Half of Watchhouse, formerly Mandolin Orange. Between band records he'd been making instrumental albums of his own, starting with Buried in a Cape in 2018.
One set: Saturday at 1 p.m. at the Windmill. He also hosted Saturday's Curation dinner with chef Jimmy Askren of Bellwether Bar.
His first Grammy nomination came that winter, Best Bluegrass Album for Mighty Poplar. Watchhouse released "Rituals" in May 2025.
Jon Middleton and Sierra Lundy, a couple from Victoria, B.C. The Junos nominated them for Breakthrough Group of the Year in 2022.
Two sets: Friday at 7 p.m. in the Woods and Saturday at 4 p.m. in the Lucky Barn.
Four months after the farm they sold out the Orpheum in Vancouver and called it the biggest show they'd ever done. Two sold-out nights at the Royal Theatre in Victoria followed.
more: In 2025 they toured Europe in theatre-size rooms and played Bonnaroo and Telluride Bluegrass.

story.t: A Brooklyn band that calls its sound discodelic soul, named as a nod to Nile Rodgers. Silver, the record that made their name, was still two months away.
Three sets: Thursday at 7 p.m. at Cherry Hill, Thursday at 11 p.m. at the Edge and midnight Friday night at the Paddock. Oregon ArtsWatch wrote that "Astral Plane" became the song of the weekend.
Silver came out that September. KCRW made it album of the year, and WXPN named them an Artist to Watch.
more: Their third album, Cut & Rewind, came out in October 2025.

story.t: An East Tennessee bluegrass band out of the Smoky Mountains, with a Best Bluegrass Album Grammy nomination for Toil, Tears & Trouble and IBMA honors behind them.

Three sets: Thursday at 1 p.m. in the Pumphouse, Thursday at 4 p.m. in the Grove and Friday at 5 p.m. at Cherry Hill. Their third Pickathon in five years. Oregon ArtsWatch heard the Cherry Hill set as a nod to the festival's own roots.
A Deep cut in 2019 and again in 2023. The Grammy nomination landed in between.
An East LA soul band led by Joey Quiñones, on Colemine Records, that had grown from four players into eleven, horns and all.
Three sets: Thursday at 11 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn, 1 a.m. Thursday night at the Edge and Friday at 11 p.m. at Cherry Hill. They come back in 2026.
Their second album, Love Stories, came out on Colemine in 2026, led by the single "Did Ya Know?"
A Richmond, Virginia band that blends jazz with hip-hop and funk, ten albums deep and on Concord Jazz. They played an NPR Tiny Desk (Home) Concert in 2021.
Three sets: Saturday at 1:45 p.m. on the Slab, Saturday at 3 p.m. at the Windmill and midnight Sunday night at the Paddock.
Solar Music won the Newlin Music Prize in 2024. Letters from the Atlantic followed in 2025, with Yaya Bey, Melanie Charles and Nicholas Payton.
Chicago's alt-glam trio. Flower of Devotion earned Pitchfork Best New Music in 2020, and Blue Skies came out on Fat Possum in 2022.
Three sets: Thursday at 6:30 p.m. on the Slab, Thursday at 10 p.m. at the Paddock and Friday at 11 p.m. in the Woods. Oregon ArtsWatch came away won over, mostly by Emily Kempf's voice.
Poetry came out in 2024.
Emily Sprague's band. Emily Alone earned Pitchfork Best New Music in 2019, and the self-titled double album followed in 2022 to wide praise.
Three sets: Friday at 8 p.m. at the Paddock, Saturday at noon on the Slab and Saturday at 9 p.m. in the Woods.
Jellywish came out on Double Double Whammy in April 2025.
A Boston band leading the traditional blues revival, with three straight number-one debuts on the Billboard blues chart in 2020, 2021 and 2022.
Three sets: Saturday at 5 p.m. in the Pumphouse, Saturday at 7 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn and Sunday at 9 p.m. at Cherry Hill.
They kept winning Blues Artist of the Year at the Boston Music Awards, in 2023, 2024 and 2025.
A Memphis bassist, famous on YouTube and in bright neon, who played with Prince in 2015 and 2016.

Three sets: Saturday at 9 p.m. at the Edge, Saturday at 11 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn and Sunday at 11 p.m. in the Woods. The Portland Mercury put his funk-jazz-rock finale in the Galaxy Barn among its favorite moments of the weekend.

Four childhood friends from Lima who join Afro-Peruvian music with DJ culture. Coba Coba was nominated for a Latin Grammy, and they'd already played Central Park SummerStage, Montreal Jazz Fest, WOMAD and Roskilde.
Three sets: Saturday at 7 p.m. at the Edge, midnight Saturday night at the Paddock and Sunday at 11 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn. Oregon ArtsWatch called the Paddock set a highlight of the weekend.
A one-man dub project on ATO. NPR called it a 21st-century take on classic dub, and The Return of... made NPR's best Latin music of 2021.
Three sets: Friday at 2 p.m. in the Grove, Friday at 7 p.m. at the Edge and Saturday at 5 p.m. at Cherry Hill.
Switched-On came out that September, then Another Place in 2025.
The son of Ali Farka Touré, called the Hendrix of the Sahara, with a Songlines Music Awards nomination for Les Racines that same year.
Three sets: Saturday at 11 p.m. in the Woods, 1 a.m. Saturday night at the Edge and Sunday at 7 p.m. at Cherry Hill. His second Pickathon, ten years after the first.
We booked her in January. In February she won the Grammy for Best Folk Album for Revealer.
more: She'd played a Tiny Desk and Jimmy Kimmel Live the summer before, and headlined the Fox Theater in Boulder.

story.t: Two sets: Saturday at 10 p.m. at the Paddock and Sunday at 7 p.m. in the Woods.
"Inventing the Wheel" picked up another Grammy nomination in 2024, Cunningham Bird with Andrew Bird came out that fall, and Ace followed in October 2025.
Ozark croon and whistle out of Fayetteville, from a former punk drummer who went viral on YouTube in 2020 and co-founded Gar Hole Records.
Two sets: 1 a.m. Friday night in the Galaxy Barn and Saturday at 6 p.m. in the Lucky Barn.
All Bad came out a month later, his first time on the Billboard charts. In 2025 he headlined the Gothic Theatre in Denver, and Refugia Blues came out that Halloween.
Dre and Vonne, friends since their teens in Tampa. They signed to Jagjaguwar in 2021, and Finally, New made DJ Mag's albums of 2022.
Three sets: Friday at 6:30 p.m. on the Slab, Friday at 11 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn and Sunday at 3 p.m. in the Woods.
The next February they opened for Wednesday in Florida: two 2023 Pickathon acts on one bill. Wish You Were Here... came out in 2024.
Ryan Kaiser's bedroom project from small-town Mississippi. "YKWIM?" had already gone platinum when we booked him.
Three sets: Thursday at 3 p.m. at the Windmill, Friday at 5 p.m. in the Pumphouse and Friday at 7 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn.
Rufus came out in 2024 and Rule of Thirds in 2025.
A Korean-American country-blues singer and poet, signed to Dan Auerbach's Easy Eye Sound.
Three sets: Thursday at 2 p.m. in the Grove, Sunday at noon in the Pumphouse and Sunday at 4 p.m. in the Lucky Barn.
NPR's World Cafe featured Yellow Peril in January 2024, and he made his national TV debut on PBS NewsHour.
An Austin guitarist and singer who made her national TV debut on Austin City Limits in 2020. That January she'd sold out Antone's every Saturday of the month.
Three sets: Thursday at 5 p.m. at Cherry Hill, Thursday at 9 p.m. at the Edge and Friday at noon in the Galaxy Barn.
The Antone's residency became a yearly thing, and The Love Anthology came out in 2025.
A singer who builds whole songs out of her own voice. Pitchfork named her a Rising artist, and her debut album came out that May.
Three sets: Friday at noon in the Pumphouse, Friday at 4 p.m. in the Lucky Barn and 1 a.m. Saturday night at Cherry Hill.
"Run" made Rolling Stone's 100 best songs of 2023. Scorpio came out in 2025, and she's on Tyler, the Creator's Don't Tap the Glass.
A Seattle soul multi-instrumentalist who grew up playing church organ in Kansas City, signed to Stone Gossard's Loosegroove Records. Her 2022 Tiny Desk (Home) Concert had a six-woman band.
Two sets: Friday at 9 p.m. at the Edge and Saturday at 3 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn.
Percussionist and vibraphonist Mike Dillon, who's played with Les Claypool, Galactic and Ani DiFranco, leading his own New Orleans punk-jazz band.
Three sets: Friday at 9 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn, Friday at 11 p.m. at the Edge and Saturday at noon in the Grove.
A producer and DJ, a new voice in hybrid dance music.
Two sets: Saturday at 2 p.m. in the Grove and 1 a.m. Sunday night in the Galaxy Barn. Oregon ArtsWatch saw him close the Galaxy Barn into the early morning.
Nashville veteran Michael Ruth, who turned to composing ambient music in 2018.

Three sets: Friday at 3 p.m. on the Slab, Friday at 7 p.m. at Cherry Hill and Sunday at 5 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn. The Portland Mercury called the early-evening Cherry Hill set an excellent psych-jazz-prog set, one of its favorite moments.
A songwriter of wide-open country and quiet places. Her self-titled debut came out on LaHonda Records in 2021, and GRAMMY.com called it powerful.
Two sets: Friday at 2 p.m. in the Lucky Barn and Saturday at 11 a.m. in the Woods.
A Portland krautrock band, together since 2012 and known for fog and lasers.
Three sets: Thursday at 2 p.m. on the Slab, Thursday at 9 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn and Sunday at 1 p.m. at the Windmill. Their second Pickathon.
An Oakland band built on Malian singer Mariam Diakite and guitarist Erich Huffaker, playing a 1970s Mali orchestra sound. They've stayed independent on purpose.
Two sets: Friday at 11 a.m. at the Windmill and Saturday at 4 p.m. in the Grove.
A Toronto garage-punk band, together since 2015.

Three sets: Friday at 1:30 p.m. on the Slab, Friday at 4 p.m. in the Grove and 1 a.m. Saturday night in the Galaxy Barn. The Portland Mercury made the Grove set a favorite moment: energetic, stranger as it went, and now a go-to.
Super Mega Ultra came out in spring 2024.
A Portland rock band, together since 2006, that has toured almost every state.
Three sets: Friday at 1 p.m. at the Windmill, Friday at 3 p.m. in the Pumphouse and Sunday at 6 p.m. in the Lucky Barn.
Brothers from the Sonoran Desert, making garage-punk noise on both sides of the border since 2017.
Four sets: Thursday at 5 p.m. on the Slab, Thursday at 9 p.m. at Cherry Hill, Sunday at 3 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn and Sunday at 5 p.m. in the Pumphouse.
A Seattle basement band born in early COVID, with members of The Moondoggies and Chris King & The Gutterballs.
Three sets: Friday at 1:30 p.m. in the Pumphouse, Friday at 5 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn and Sunday at noon in the Grove.
A tabla, fiddle and guitar trio. Their debut, bloom, came out that February.
Three sets: Saturday at 11 a.m. at the Windmill, Saturday at 1:30 p.m. in the Pumphouse and Sunday at 2 p.m. in the Lucky Barn.
Folk-rock brothers from southeast Kentucky, playing since 2010.
Two sets: Friday at 11 a.m. in the Woods and Sunday at 3 p.m. at the Windmill.
Sunny Faris of Blackwater Holylight and Cameron Spies of Night Heron, making Portland shoegaze and synth-pop.
Four sets: Thursday at 1 p.m. at the Windmill, Thursday at 3:30 p.m. on the Slab, Sunday at 1 p.m. in the Galaxy Barn and Sunday at 3 p.m. in the Pumphouse.

archCT.l: Portland old-time players who played punk-fast and made records for eMpTy.

They formed in Greenwich Village in 1963, gave freak folk its name, put a song on the Easy Rider soundtrack, kept Sam Shepard on drums before he won the Pulitzer, moved to Portland and broke up in 1978. They got back together in 1999. That was the year of the first Pickathon, and they spent it on our stage.

archCT.l: A Rounder-signed Cajun and old-time multi-instrumentalist, with a young Cajun star beside him.

A California fiddler and singer who had already won the bluegrass world's highest honors by the time she came to the second Pickathon, and who played it with Tom Rozum, the mandolin player she had been sharing a stage and a microphone with for years.
Portland's decorated acoustic blues guitarist, who produced John Fahey.
A Northwest protest-folk songwriter, signed to Appleseed before he played Pickathon.
The Cajun crew returned a year later with friends.
The fiddler the National Endowment for the Arts calls synonymous with Irish fiddle music worldwide - a Bothy Band founder who has lived in Portland since 1979.

archCT.n: danny barnes and the piano throwers
CJ Chenier & the Red Hot Louisiana Band

archCT.l: He toured steadily the year before Pendarvis and the year he came - opera houses in small towns, the Old Town School in Chicago, a folk circuit he had worked for thirty years. Then it stopped: by 2024 he had all but come off the road. Pickathon caught the last full stretch of a working life on the road.

She plays more often now than the year before Pendarvis, and in bigger rooms. Two decades after the farm, at an age when most of her peers have come off the road, she is busier than she was when we booked her.
Portland folk band that played Pickathon the year before it signed to Kill Rock Stars.
Accordion busker from Everett who turned a vodka-bottle percussion act into a travelling river circus.
Pennsylvania songwriter whom Entertainment Weekly called 'your next obsession' the year after Pickathon.
Austin's long-running swamp-folk band whose 'Gin and Juice' cover outlived the band's hiatus.
A husband-and-wife gothic-country duo from 1993 whose murder ballad became the opening titles of True Detective seven years after they played here.

archCT.n: The Reverend Peyton's Big Damn Band
archCT.l: Indiana washboard-and-shotgun-guitar trio that played Pickathon the year of its gospel tin and went on to top Billboard's blues chart.
New York busking duo that played Pickathon on its first tour.
Duluth string band whose albums went from not charting at Pickathon 2007 to number one on the bluegrass chart.
Austin's punk-bluegrass originals - banjo covers of punk songs, a debut produced by a Butthole Surfer, and a tour with them to match.
Boston string band that rebuilt its lineup in January 2008 and later turned up in The Last of Us.
An Oklahoma Choctaw songwriter on the Avett Brothers' label, who won Native American Music Awards for both album and songwriter the same year she played here.
Seattle trio from the ashes of Pretty Girls Make Graves, signed to Matador months before Pickathon 2008.
A W.C. Handy best-new-artist winner who had been playing country blues for thirteen years by the time he got to the farm.
A 21-year-old California rockabilly institution that now sings in a Disney bear show.
Portland band that Rolling Stone ranked No. 13 album of 2008, then Pickathon, Coachella and Bonnaroo in a year.
An Australian ragtime-blues showman who won the ARIA for blues the year he reached Pickathon.
A Philadelphia band that signed to Anti- the summer it played the farm, already filling Fillmores. They retired from touring in 2021 and came back for Red Rocks.
A Toronto 'death country' trio shortlisted for the Polaris Prize the year it played Pickathon.
A Chicago carpenter who gave away 15,000 CDs and went on tour with Steve Earle.
The founder of Los Angeles punk's X, 33 years in when he reached Pickathon.
A Cajun band that has won the Grammy twice since its Pickathon debut.

Two of bluegrass's most respected instrumentalists, billed together: a flatpicker voted the best guitar player in bluegrass three years running, and the mandolinist who founded the Nashville Bluegrass Band and shaped the sound of the O Brother soundtrack.

archCT.n: Thao & The Get Down Stay Down

archCT.l: A Saskatoon folk band whose 2009 breakout won Canada's folk and western awards.
Chris Thile's string band, playing small rooms in 2010, ended up with a Grammy and a Red Rocks co-headline.
A Smog veteran whose Apocalypse tour landed on three year-end lists the year he played.

archCT.n: Lost Bayou Ramblers ft Gordon Gano

archCT.l: Hand-built banjo and guitar duo from Horsefly, B.C. who went on to win four Junos.
Seattle duo that Sub Pop signed as its first hip-hop act and whose debut topped half a dozen best-of-the-year lists.
A one-man band with a suitcase kick drum who sold out two small Denver clubs in April 2014 and headlined Red Rocks not long after.
A Brooklyn singer-songwriter whose Tramp sold out the Bowery Ballroom and landed on year-end lists the year before Pickathon.

Hardly anything on the books in 2012: a bar in Austin and a basement room in Nashville. He came to the farm the next summer as his first solo record landed - though he had already played it in 2011, fronting a band called Sunday Valley. Ten years on he was playing Hampton Coliseum and Bridgestone Arena.
Dallas gospel-funk brothers who vanished for thirty years, then came back with a Jim Eno-produced album that NPR and the New York Times covered.
Her first full-band record had NPR, A.V. Club and Pitchfork behind it, and three years later she sold out Brooklyn Steel.
She played the big stage at dusk, then a packed barn an hour later, and a little over a year after that she was a Grammy nominee.
A Colorado farmer-songwriter who climbed from NPR studio sessions to two sold-out nights at Red Rocks.
A North Carolina songwriter whose 2014 Merge debut landed on NPR, Uncut and American Songwriter year-end lists.
A goofy Montreal slacker-rock songwriter who went from club nights to three sold-out nights at the Greek.
Platinum-selling Grammy winners who reunited the same year they headlined Pickathon.

Two albums out that almost nobody had rated, and almost nothing on the calendar the year he came to the farm. Nobody had reviewed him. Now he headlines arenas, his records draw strong reviews, and he has played a Tiny Desk - but in nineteen years of critics' year-end lists his name has never once been ranked.
Tuva's throat-singing masters, 25 years in, reaching the farm.
The Dinosaur Jr. guitarist alone with an acoustic guitar.
The Chicago guitarist the best songwriters call, stepping out with his first record.
NJ band that toured nonstop the year Cardinal broke.
A 1990s indie landmark from Boise, 26 years on, playing the Pickathon woods.
A Texas road dog playing clubs in 2018 who sold out the Ryman four years later.
Haley Fohr's baritone art-song project, an acclaimed cult act who came to the woods in 2018.
A Saskatchewan baritone whose clubs in 2018 became sold-out theaters, the Ryman included.
A Kyiv folk-punk quartet that Bonnaroo and the Kennedy Center had already made world-music royalty.
A banjo innovator who won Steve Martin's prize, here with a new trio.
An Ethiopian jazz-funk pioneer who drove a cab around Dulles until a reissue rediscovered him.
A Portland songwriter whose debut won Pitchfork and a Tiny Desk the summer she played.
Two Asheville musicians who rework old hymns on fiddle and guitar.
Three roots stars in one band, a Grammy winner two years later.
A Chicago poet-singer whose Heavn made Pitchfork's 2016 top 40.
Australia's Double J Artist of the Year, on the American road in 2018.
Nashville's Mr. Jukebox, a Broadway fiddler turned Third Man debut artist.
An Anacortes K Records lifer who once mailed a new record to subscribers every month.
A Tokyo psych band that built an audience abroad and took its last bow in 2022.

archCT.n: Phil Lesh & The Terrapin Family Band

archCT.l: He played Pickathon between a bar in Brussels and a back room in Amsterdam. The next year he made one of the most acclaimed records in the country, and he has been headlining his own rooms on three continents since.
They played their first US shows in December 2021, came to the farm in August 2022, and won two Grammys the next February.
A Seattle singer on Stone Gossard's label whose Tiny Desk home concert reached NPR listeners in 2022.
Booked in January, she won the Grammy for Best Folk Album the next month.
The year before Pickathon he was playing small rooms under his own name and opening for Plains in the big ones. Two years after, he headlined the Ryman.

The only show on their record the year before Pickathon was at a public library in Hoover, Alabama. They have a full calendar booked for next year. Whether the rooms grow with the schedule is the open question about them.
Adi Oasis was already headlining Paris rooms like La Cigale and playing North Sea Jazz when Pickathon booked her.
Anna Tivel came to Pickathon after NPR Music named her album Outsiders the best roots music of 2022 and gave her a Tiny Desk.
Billie Marten came to Pickathon after Drop Cherries drew rave reviews and took No. 5 on The Independent's best albums of 2023.
Daniel Villarreal is a Panama-born drummer whose 2022 debut Panama 77 drew reviews from Fader, the Chicago Tribune and Aquarium Drunkard.
Dean Johnson played Pickathon in 2024 and finished the year opening for John Craigie at Revolution Hall in Portland.
Durand Jones came to Pickathon off Wait Til I Get Over, a 2023 solo album that drew universal acclaim.
Elephant Revival came to Pickathon as a Colorado folk band that had closed Red Rocks in 2018 and reunited in 2022.
Ellis Bullard came to Pickathon as the hot thing in Austin's honky-tonks, with two strong Saving Country Music reviews behind him.
Erin Rae came to Pickathon with Newport Folk and a spot on Tyler Childers' Rustin' in the Rain behind her.
Florry is a Philadelphia alt-country band whose 2023 album The Holey Bible was Stereogum's Album of the Week.
Geese played Pickathon in the middle of a climb from small clubs to opening for Greta Van Fleet in arenas.
Irreversible Entanglements came to Pickathon off Protect Your Light, an Impulse! record that jazz critics put at or near the top of their 2023 lists.
J.D. Simo is a guitar-world favorite who plays his own shows in clubs and sits in as special guest in the big halls.
Jake Kohn is a young songwriter who spent the spring before Pickathon opening for Sierra Ferrell in clubs and theaters.
Jeffrey Martin came to Pickathon from Portland off Thank God We Left the Garden, a 2023 album that drew universal acclaim.
Jess Williamson came to Pickathon with Time Ain't Accidental on more than a dozen 2023 year-end lists, including No. 2 on Stereogum's country list.
Joanna Sternberg came to Pickathon with I've Got Me on thirteen ranked 2023 year-end lists, best at No. 7 on Far Out's.
John Haywood is the Kentucky old-time banjo player on Tyler Childers' 'Long Violent History'.
Kara Jackson came to Pickathon with one of the most praised albums of 2023, a Pitchfork Best New Music pick, and was still headlining small rooms.
Kassa Overall came to Pickathon after Animals hit No. 1 on KEXP's chart and earned him a second NPR Tiny Desk.
In 2024, the year LA LOM played Pickathon, the Los Angeles band opened for Cory Wong in theaters and for Vampire Weekend in amphitheaters.
McKinley Dixon came to Pickathon with Beloved! Paradise! Jazz!? ranked No. 3 on Paste's best albums of 2023.
Melissa Carper, an Austin upright bassist, came to Pickathon with Rolling Stone and the Boston Globe already on her side and a new album, Borned in Ya, on the way.
Mitchum Yacoub leads a San Diego Afrobeat and cumbia band, Brass Empire, that put out its debut LP on All-Town Sound in 2023.
Pahua is the Mexico City project of Paulina Sotomayor, and KEXP and Rolling Stone en Espanol covered her before and around Pickathon.
Ratboys came to Pickathon with The Window ranked No. 1 by Treble and by Under the Radar on 2023's year-end lists.
Rhododendron, a Portland trio that started at School of Rock in 2019, got a Willamette Week feature the spring before Pickathon.
Sami Braman is an old-time fiddler with The Onlies who made her solo debut, Riveter, in 2023.
Searows played Pickathon in 2024 and finished the year opening for Robin Pecknold at the Aladdin Theater in Portland.
Sluice is a Durham, North Carolina band whose album Radial Gate made The Guardian's best albums of 2023 so far.
The Soul Rebels came to Pickathon thirty-three years into a New Orleans brass band career that took them to Bonnaroo, Tokyo and four nights opening for Metallica.
Theo Lawrence was selling out Paris clubs years before Pickathon.
This Is Lorelei played Pickathon with no real room history behind it, then went out as support to DEHD at Brooklyn Steel that October.
True Loves is a Seattle band whose 2018 KEXP session passed two million YouTube views.
Two Runner is a Nevada City duo, Paige Anderson and Emilie Rose, who spent most of 2023 on the road.
Vincent Neil Emerson came to Pickathon already opening in rooms like Red Rocks, while his own headline shows ran in small clubs.
Water From Your Eyes were still headlining small clubs when Pickathon booked them, and in 2024 they were opening for Squid and Real Estate in theaters.
